# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)

- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

## 这是什么

原站是ギア（@giaaibusi）发布的三大 AI 绘画参考图库（姿势、服装、人像），元数据全部为日文，且分散在三个独立站点。本仓库（v2.0）完成了**三站合一、全量中文化、AI 角色合成工作台与 ComfyUI 原生插件升级**：

1. **三库四站全量本地镜像（11,568 张图）** —— 完整收录姿势库（素体白模 2,878 张 + 深度图 Depth 2,878 张 WebP）、服装库（2,814 张 WebP）、人像库（2,998 张，全尺寸 `1600×2000` 高清 WebP）的全部缩略图与高清原图，支持纯离线浏览与静态托管。
2. **100% 纯净中文元数据（零日文残留）** —— 动作体系、姿势分类、服装款式、穿搭标签、人像分区、发长与 51 种细分发型全部译为地道中文，自动组装的生图提示词纯净无日文干扰。
3. **三合一 AI 角色合成工作台（Web Studio）** —— 基于 **React 19 + Tailwind CSS 4 + TypeScript 7 + shadcn/ui + TanStack Router** 构建的响应式多页面应用（兼容 PC / 平板 / 手机）：
   - 从三大图库任意挑选 **人像 + 服装 + 姿势（支持素体白模 / 深度图一键切换）** 组合配方，或一键随机捏人；
   - 支持拖拽、剪贴板粘贴（`Cmd+V` / `Ctrl+V`）或 URL 添加多张自定义附加参考图；
   - 内置 **5 大 AI 图像协议直连**（Google Gemini、OpenAI GPT Image、阿里云百炼 Qwen、字节火山方舟 Doubao、**本地 ComfyUI**），生成记录通过 **IndexedDB** 本地持久化保存。
4. **原生 ComfyUI 自定义节点插件（`custom_nodes`）** —— 本仓库同时是一个即插即用的 ComfyUI 插件！直接 `git clone` 到 `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/` 即可在 ComfyUI 画布内使用 **姿势 / 服装 / 人像 / 三合一角色配方** 4 个自定义节点（姿势与配方节点内置 `use_depth` 深度图切换，可直接接入 ControlNet Depth）与内置的 **4,345 条中文可视化弹窗选图器**。

---

## 核心功能

### 1. 三大参考图库（姿势 / 服装 / 人像）
- **姿势参考库（`/poses`）**：4 大体系（全身单人・标准系 / 全身单人・性感系 / 上半身单人 / 双人缠绵）、26 个动作分类、288 组姿势、5 种视角（正面 / 斜前 / 侧面 / 背面 / 俯视），支持**按姿势分组 / 逐张浏览**双模式、卡片内多角度切换，以及 **`[ 素体白模 | 深度图 (Depth) ]` 一键切换预览与下载**。
- **服装参考库（`/costumes`）**：8 大穿搭分类（春季 / 夏季 / 秋季 / 冬季 / 内衣・睡衣 / 性感穿搭 / 泳装・度假 / 派对・礼服）、86 个中文细节标签与英文 Prompt 关键词。
- **人像参考库（`/portraits`）**：2 大分区（正脸参考 893 / 造型氛围 606）、4 种发长（短发 / 中发 / 中长发 / 长发）、51 种细分发型，支持**精选题集**与**热门榜单**一键筛选。
- **统一交互体验**：中文关键词实时检索、灯箱高清原图预览与下载、一键「加入合成配方」。

### 2. AI 角色合成台（`/studio`）
- **3+N 参考图组合**：3 个核心槽位（人像 / 服装 / 姿势，姿势槽位内置 `[ 白模 | 深度 ]` 实时切换）+ 任意张自定义附加参考图（点击上传、拖拽文件、剪贴板粘贴、填写图片 URL）。
- **参考拼图预览与导出**：弹窗查看三合一高清参考拼图（`1800×1200` Canvas 实时合成），支持一键下载拼图 PNG。
- **12 种画风预设 & 纯中文结构化提示词**：内置「无预设（跟随参考图）」、写实人像写真、日韩杂志画报、复古胶片写真、2.5D 游戏原画立绘、日系二次元插画、新海诚感动画电影、日式黑白漫画网点、3D 次世代角色渲染、3D 潮玩手办质感、赛博朋克霓虹、角色设定集立绘（纯白底）共 12 种画风，根据已选素材自动组装提示词。
- **5 大 AI 图像协议与高级参数**：
  - **Google Gemini**：`gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview`、`gemini-3-pro-image-preview`、`gemini-2.5-flash-image`（支持宽高比 `aspectRatio`、分辨率 `1K/2K/4K`）
  - **OpenAI GPT Image**：`gpt-image-2.5`、`gpt-image-2`、`gpt-image-1.5`、`gpt-image-1`（支持 `/v1/images/edits` JSON URL 直传 / Multipart 上传、尺寸、质量、背景透明度）
  - **阿里云百炼 Qwen**：`qwen-image-3.0-pro`、`qwen-image-2.1-pro`、`qwen-image-2.0-pro`、`qwen-image-edit-plus`（支持 `multimodal-generation` 多图参考输入、智能改写 `prompt_extend`、水印开关）
  - **字节火山方舟 Doubao**：`doubao-seedream-5-0`、`doubao-seedream-4-5-251128`、`doubao-seedream-4-0-250828`、`doubao-seededit-3-0-i2i-250628`（支持多图融合 `image: [...]`、2K/4K 分辨率）
  - **本地 ComfyUI 工作流引擎**：支持自动将三合一拼图及单张人像/服装/姿势图上传至本地 ComfyUI（`/upload/image`），注入自定义 API 工作流占位符或自动识别节点提交 `/prompt` 队列并轮询取回成品图；支持导入/导出通用 `.api.json` 工作流模板。
- **跨页面后台生图 & IndexedDB 历史记录**：切换页面不会中断正在进行的生图请求；生成结果自动存入浏览器 IndexedDB（避免 `localStorage` 容量限制），支持复用提示词与原图下载。

> 本地 ComfyUI 三图合成（Qwen Image Edit 2509）的模型清单、工作流说明和本地运行方法见 [docs/comfyui-local.md](docs/comfyui-local.md)。

> 导入 API 后的动态高级参数、设定集参考上传与可选显示声明见 [ComfyUI 工作流高级参数](docs/comfyui-workflow-parameters.md)。

### 3. ComfyUI 原生自定义节点插件（`comfyui_plugin/`）
将本仓库克隆到 `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/ai-pose-gallery-zh` 后，ComfyUI 画布右键菜单 **「AI角色三合一参考图集」** 下自动提供 4 个节点：
- **AI 姿势参考图 (`PoseGalleryNode`)**：输出 `姿势图 (IMAGE)`、`图片ID`、`姿势提示词`（支持 `use_depth` 开关一键切换输出素体白模或深度图）
- **AI 服装参考图 (`CostumeGalleryNode`)**：输出 `服装图 (IMAGE)`、`图片ID`、`中文服装描述`、`英文服装Prompt`
- **AI 人像参考图 (`PortraitGalleryNode`)**：输出 `人像图 (IMAGE)`、`图片ID`、`人像发型描述`
- **AI 角色三合一合成配方 (`CharacterRecipeNode`)**：单节点同时输出 `人像图`、`服装图`、`姿势图（支持 use_depth 深度图切换）`、`三合一拼图` 以及自动组装的 `中文合成Prompt` 与 `英文合成Prompt`，并内置 **4,345 条中文可视化弹窗选图器（含 🌗 深度图预览开关）**与节点内实时缩略图预览。

## 在 ComfyUI 中使用（双模式支持）

### 模式 A：作为 ComfyUI 原生插件安装（在 ComfyUI 画布内选图）

无需安装额外 Python 依赖（直接复用 ComfyUI 自带的 `torch`、`numpy`、`Pillow`、`aiohttp`）：

```bash
cd /path/to/ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/anhao/ai-pose-gallery-zh.git
```

重启 ComfyUI 后：
1. 在画布空白处右键 → **新建节点** → **AI角色三合一参考图集**；
2. 选择 **「AI 角色三合一合成配方 (3-in-1 Recipe)」** 或单个姿势 / 服装 / 人像节点；
3. 点击节点上的 **「🎨 打开三合一选图器 (4,345张)」** 按钮（或直接点击节点上的缩略图），即可在弹窗中按分类、视角、发长筛选或中文搜索，一键填入节点并输出 `IMAGE` 张量与中英文 Prompt。

### 模式 B：从 Web 合成台直连本地 ComfyUI API

如果您使用线上网页端（或本地 `pnpm dev`）选图，希望直接调用本机 ComfyUI 生图：
1. 启动本地 ComfyUI 时开启跨域参数：
   ```bash
   python main.py --enable-cors-header "*"
   ```
2. 打开本工作台 **「接口配置」** 页面 → 切换到 **「本地 ComfyUI」** → 点击「检测连接」（默认 `http://127.0.0.1:8188`）；
3. 可直接导入您在 ComfyUI 中通过 `工作流 -> 导出 (API)` 保存的 `.json` 文件（支持 `{{prompt}}`、`{{seed}}`、`{{width}}`、`{{height}}`、`{{composite_image}}`、`{{portrait_image}}`、`{{costume_image}}`、`{{pose_image}}` 占位符，或由系统自动匹配 `CLIPTextEncode` / `KSampler` / `LoadImage` 节点），也可在 **「合成台」** 一键导出内置通用工作流模板。

```bash

# 2. 启动本地开发服务器（默认 http://localhost:5173）

# 3. 类型检查 + 生产构建 + 代码规范检查
pnpm build && pnpm lint
```

### 数据与图片维护脚本（Python 3）

```bash
# 拉取/补全三站图片（已存在的文件自动跳过，支持断点续传）
python3 scripts/download.py
WORKERS=64 python3 scripts/download.py   # 调整并发线程数

## 部署到 Cloudflare（Workers / Pages）

本项目自带 [wrangler.jsonc](wrangler.jsonc) 与 [worker.ts](worker.ts)，同时支持 **Cloudflare Workers（含静态 Assets + `/api/proxy` 同源代理）** 与 **Cloudflare Pages** 部署。仓库总体积约 `1.1 GB`、总文件数约 `11,600` 个、单文件全部 `< 2 MB`，完全符合 Cloudflare 免费版限制（单文件 ≤ 25 MiB，文件数 ≤ 20,000）。

> 💡 **自定义代理域名白名单（可选）**：`/api/proxy` 默认放行五大官方 AI 接口域名，并在切换至阿里云百炼（Qwen）或火山方舟（Doubao）时自动开启。若需通过服务端代理转发自定义中转站，可在 Cloudflare 环境变量或 `wrangler.jsonc` 的 `vars.PROXY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` 中配置逗号分隔的来源白名单（支持精确域名与泛子域名，如 `https://api.example.com,https://*.openai.com`）。

### 方式一：Cloudflare Workers 自动/命令行部署（推荐，内置 `/api/proxy` 解决千问/豆包跨域）

# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code and Codex that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

# Mika **An AI assistant on your phone: say what you need, and it works your apps and the web until it's done.** It works on a hidden background screen, so you can keep using your phone. English · [简体中文](docs/readme/README.zh-CN.md) · [繁體中文](docs/readme/README.zh-Hant.md) · [日本語](docs/readme/README.ja.md) · [한국어](docs/readme/README.ko.md) · [Español](docs/readme/README.es.md)
"Send a message to File Transfer": Mika's chat on the left, each step on its background screen on the right (4× speed; chat list blurred)
## Get things done with one sentence

"What did the group talk about today?"
Scrolls through the chat in the background, then sums it up
"A charger under $30, rated 4.5 stars or more"
Adds the pick to the cart and stops before checkout
"What has this creator posted lately?"
Opens the app, reads post by post, then sums it up
More demos

Greets recruiters for 3 jobs on a job site
Finds the cheapest nonstop from San Francisco to New York
Reads out the top 5 stories on a news site

Finds jobs and greets recruiters
Watches ads to unlock music perks
Orders takeout with stacked discounts, asks before paying
Several demos use apps popular in China: WeChat is the main messaging app there, and Xiaohongshu (RED) is a lifestyle and social platform. Mika isn't tied to them; it works with any app or website on your phone. ## Why Mika | | | |---|---| | 📱 **Leaves your screen alone** | Opens apps, taps, types and scrolls on a separate background screen while you use your phone as usual; tap the small live view whenever you want to watch | | 🧩 **Works with any app** | Looks at the screen and finds buttons the way a person does: no app APIs, no per-app integration | | 🌐 **Call it from any web page** | In the built-in browser, say what you want on the page you're reading and it works right there; touch the page and it stops | | 🧠 **Gets better with use** | Remembers the preferences you tell it, and turns tasks it finishes into skills so next time is faster and steadier | | 🔒 **Your data stays on your phone** | There is no Mika server; use your own model API key, or sign in with a ChatGPT, xAI or OpenRouter account | | 🆓 **Open source and free** | Apache-2.0, all code public | ## Get started in three steps 1. **Install**: download the APK from [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases/latest). 2. **Connect a model**: in Settings › Model, pick a provider and enter an API key, or just sign in with an account ([models and sign-in](docs/models.en.md)). 3. **To operate phone apps**: follow the "Set up phone control" wizard in Settings and pair wireless debugging on the phone once ([setup guide](docs/setup-guide.en.md)). Skip this if you only want chat, web and files. Then try saying: "Set alarms for 9:40 and 10:00 tomorrow morning" or "Check the weather at 8 every morning and tell me only if it will rain". > 💡 Have a computer handy? Send this to the AI agent on it and it will set everything up for you:
> `Follow https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/blob/main/docs/install-with-agent.en.md to install Mika on the Android phone connected over USB.` ## What it can do | | | |---|---| | **Operate apps** | Reads long lists and chat histories, taps and types, shares text into apps; hands logins, verification codes and payments to you | | **Browse the web** | A built-in desktop-class browser that keeps you signed in, reads pages, downloads and uploads; paces itself and hands block pages to you | | **Your current screen** | Double-tap the floating capsule to send the screen you're looking at: "how should I reply?", "note this down" | | **Schedules and conditions** | "Remind me at 9 tomorrow", "do this every Friday"; runs on time in the original conversation | | **Jump in or stop anytime** | Keep talking while a task runs to add or correct things (long-press to withdraw or edit one Mika hasn't picked up yet); after a stop it reports where it got to, and "continue" picks up from there | | **Hold to talk** | Hold the chat input to speak and edit the words before sending; long-press the floating capsule to speak and release to send. Uses the phone’s built-in speech recognition, or a provider’s speech model if it has none | | **Files and computing** | A Linux sandbox per conversation runs Python, Node and shell on the files you send (arm64) | | **From your computer** | AI tools on your computer can hand Mika tasks through CLI + Skill or MCP ([use Mika from a computer](docs/computer.en.md)) | By default Mika runs in **Ask mode**: it checks with you only before spending money (placing orders, paying) and just does everything else. You can switch to **Autonomous mode** instead. See [Ask and Autonomous](docs/modes.en.md). For how each of these works and the finer details, see [features in detail](docs/features.en.md).
Apps and websites with built-in usage knowledge (anything not listed still works) The names are shown as they appear in the knowledge files. | Category | Built in | |---|---| | **Apps** | Android 设置, 百家号, 哔哩哔哩, BOSS直聘, Chrome, 得到, 抖音, 飞书, Gmail, 即刻, 快手, 领英, QQ邮箱, Telegram, 今日头条, Uber, Uber Eats, 微信, 微博, WhatsApp, 闲鱼, 小红书, 知乎 | | **Websites** | Amazon, 哔哩哔哩, Google Calendar, 豆瓣, 抖音, Instagram, Gmail, Google Maps, Telegram, 百度贴吧, 微博, 搜狗微信, WhatsApp, 小红书, 小宇宙, YouTube, 知乎, BOSS直聘 | | **How-to skills** | 改 Mika 自己的设置, 把内容整理成文字, 处理 PDF 文档, 查清一件事, 消息与邮件, 写技能 |
Supported model providers Presets for DeepSeek, 通义千问, Kimi, 智谱, 硅基流动, 火山方舟, MiniMax, 阶跃星辰, 腾讯混元, 百度千帆, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI, xAI, Mistral, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio and more; for any other provider pick Custom (自定义), which takes any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or OpenAI Responses endpoint. You can also skip the key and sign in with a ChatGPT (Plus / Pro), xAI / Grok or OpenRouter account. Steps for adding a model, and what to know about each sign-in, are in [models and sign-in](docs/models.en.md).
## Which phones | | Requirement | |---|---| | Chat, web, files | Android 11 or later | | Operating phone apps | Android 12 or later; **Android 14+ recommended** (the background screen has its own focus, so it doesn't get in the way of your typing on the main screen) | | Linux sandbox | arm64 devices | Not sure your phone is up to it? Run Settings › Recovery & repair › **Compatibility self-check**: 12 checks in about a minute, and you can [send us the results](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/issues/new?template=device-report.yml) in one tap. ## Privacy & safety - **There is no Mika server**: what you say and what's on your screen go only to the model provider you set up. - API keys and memories are stored encrypted on the phone; conversations and run records stay on the device; update checks only contact GitHub. - Operating third-party apps and websites automatically may break their terms of service, so use your own judgment. For anything important, use Ask mode and check the results. See the [disclaimer](docs/disclaimer.en.md).
FAQ **Wireless debugging turned itself off?** Android turns it off when you change Wi-Fi or restart. With your permission, Mika turns it back on by itself; if it still can't connect, go back to "Set up phone control" and pair again. **Can't find wireless debugging on my phone?** Some phone systems leave it out. You can start the phone helper from a computer over USB instead; see the [setup guide](docs/setup-guide.en.md). **Some screens can't be read or captured?** Pages like payments and password entry block screenshots, so Mika asks you to take over there. **Can I use a model running on my own computer?** Yes: pick "Custom" as the provider and enter its address on your local network. **Is the app in English?** Yes. The app UI comes in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian and Indonesian, follows your system language, and can be switched in Settings › Language. The built-in app and website knowledge is written in Chinese, but that doesn't limit you: the model reads it fine, and you can talk to Mika in English. **Where do updates come from?** Only from this repository's [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases); you can also upgrade in the app from About › Check for updates. More answers are in the [FAQ](docs/faq.en.md).
## Community & contributing - **Docs**: all docs and a suggested reading order are in the [docs index](docs/README.en.md) - **Community**: join the [X group chat](https://x.com/i/chat/group_join/g2116926829198246025/48B52j5svL); to reach the author on WeChat, scan the QR code in the app under About › Contact the author (mention Mika in your request) - **Follow the author**: X [@wangzan101](https://x.com/wangzan101) - **Report a problem**: [open an issue](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/issues/new/choose); About › Send feedback in the app can attach diagnostics - **Contribute**: add usage knowledge for an app or website (plain text, no code needed), or contribute code; see the [contributing guide](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Star History ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who has helped build Mika: ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE) · [NOTICE](NOTICE) · [Third-party components](licenses/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)

# TotK Recomp

**TotK Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native x86-64 application for Windows and Linux ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tears of the Kingdom*, dumped from your own console: the base game and the 1.1.0, 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.
>
> The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

## Status

Early development. The game is playable on Windows and Linux; visual bugs and crashes are still expected.

Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Features

- Native code, not emulation
- Game updates 1.1.0, 1.2.1 and 1.4.3; 1.2.1 and 1.4.3 saves carry over between them
- 60 fps by default; up to 144 fps or the monitor's refresh rate (experimental)
- Custom resolutions (1080p, 2k...), supersampling and AMD FSR 1 upscaling
- HDR10 output with peak, game and HUD brightness settings
- 16:10 (Steam Deck, handhelds), 21:9 and 32:9 (ultrawide) game resolutions, with the camera and the interface in that shape
- Anisotropic texture filtering up to 16x, for sharp ground into the distance
- In-game settings menu (F1) and performance overlay (F10)
- Setup and in-game menu in English, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese
- Keyboard, mouse and gamepad with remapping, rumble and gyro
- Xbox button prompts: LB, RB, LT, RT, Menu and View, and A, B, X and Y as labelled on the button to press, with either button layout
- Shaders prepared at install instead of during play
- Mods made for emulators: unpack a mod into the `mods` folder next to `totk.exe`; switch and order them in the menu. RomFS
  mods, TKMM's merged output and ExeFS code patches (`.ips`, `.pchtxt`) work; the game rebuilds itself for code patches
  ([docs/tester-guide.md](docs/tester-guide.md), "Mods")
- Atmosphère cheats: put a cheat file into a mod and switch its cheats in the menu ([docs/cheats.md](docs/cheats.md))

## Planned

- VRR

## Installing

### Windows

Requirements: Windows 10 or later, an x86-64 CPU with SSE4.2 (AVX2/FMA machines get a faster build), a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`, about 36 GiB free during setup (20 GiB after).

1. Download `TotK-Setup-<version>-windows.zip` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and unpack it.
2. Start `TotK-Setup.exe`. If SmartScreen warns about an unsigned app, choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
3. Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press *Start*. The setup builds the game once.
4. Play `totk.exe` from the install folder.

### Linux

Requirements: as on Windows, plus Linux 6.7 or later and glibc 2.34 or later (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 35, SteamOS 3).

1. Download `TotK-Setup-x86_64.AppImage` from [Releases](../../releases/latest), or build it ([docs/installer.md](docs/installer.md), "Linux release").
2. Make it executable (`chmod +x TotK-Setup-x86_64.AppImage`) and start it. On a Steam Deck, do this in Desktop Mode.
3. Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press *Start*.
4. Play `totk` from the install folder.

To update, run a newer setup on the same folder; saves and settings are kept. Settings are in the in-game menu and in `totk.ini` ([totk.ini.example](totk.ini.example) lists every key). Controls: [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md).

## Credits

TotK Recomp builds on the projects below. What was taken from each, with its license, is listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

- [LAS Recomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp)
- [MacNativeGames](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames)
- [d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile) and [nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)
- [SavageWindRecomp](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp)
- [Ryujinx](https://github.com/Ryujinx/Ryujinx)
- [deko3d](https://github.com/devkitPro/deko3d)
- [hactool](https://github.com/SciresM/hactool)
- [SDL 3](https://libsdl.org), [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), [AMD FSR 1](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Effects/FidelityFX-FSR), [Vulkan Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator), [libopus](https://opus-codec.org), [libvpx](https://chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libvpx), [Zstandard](https://github.com/facebook/zstd)
- [Switchbrew](https://switchbrew.org) and the Switch homebrew community

## License

The project's own code is under the [MIT License](LICENSE); third-party code keeps its own license ([THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)). The license grants nothing for Nintendo's game.

TotK Recomp is an independent, non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. *The Legend of Zelda*, *Tears of the Kingdom* and *Nintendo Switch* are trademarks of Nintendo.

## Building from source

[docs/building.md](docs/building.md) lists the toolchain and the steps. Everything the build writes stays under `build\` and `generated\`, which git ignores; run `tools/check_content.py` before a commit. Testers: [docs/tester-guide.md](docs/tester-guide.md).

# pixelfx. **244 pixel art effects and animations, every one a small piece of code.** Fire, explosions, magic, weather, UI, pickups, critters and more. Plus a Claude Code skill that makes new ones the way a picky pixel artist would: draft, render, look, refine. Every effect that involves a character is **acted out**: he winds up, lets go, freezes on contact and recovers, and a target takes the hit. Twelve whole moves chain the effects into attacks from wind-up to recovery. **[open the gallery](https://patch-gg.github.io/pixelfx/)** · [catalog](docs/CATALOG.md) · [acting](#acting) · [the skill](#the-skill) · [make your own](#make-your-own) · [how it works](#how-it-works) The method is [Hugo Duprez](https://x.com/HugoDuprez)'s, from [How to make (good) pixel art effects with Claude](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/how-to-make-good-pixel-art-effects-with-claude): code is clay, trust your eyes, feed your references. His [open-source effects](https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-art-vfx) at Sprite Fusion set the bar, and `src/core/sim.js` and the effects that say so at the top adapt his code. This repo is our take on the idea at library scale, with a skill to keep going. ## what's in it. | category | effects | some of them | |---|---|---| | **moves** | 12 | arrow shot, dash strike, earth stomp, fireball throw, ground pound, holy smite… | | **fire** | 12 | brazier, campfire, candle, fire breath, fire ring, fire tornado… | | **explosions** | 12 | barrel explosion, big explosion, cartoon pow, dirt explosion, firework burst, firework rocket… | | **water** | 12 | bubbles, drip, fountain, geyser, rain splash, ripples… | | **ice** | 10 | blizzard vortex, freeze, frost breath, frost nova, ice crystal, ice lance… | | **lightning** | 11 | ball lightning, chain lightning, charge up, electrified, lightning strike, plasma ball… | | **sci-fi** | 12 | emp blast, energy core, force field, glitch, hologram, jetpack… | | **melee** | 12 | claw swipe, dagger flurry, double slash, hammer smash, heavy cleave, scythe reap… | | **impacts** | 11 | blunt hit, bullet impact, critical hit, ground slam, heavy landing, hit flash… | | **projectiles** | 13 | arrow, bullet tracer, cannon shot, energy disc, signal flare, homing missile… | | **spawn & death** | 10 | coin drop, disintegrate, dissolve burn, egg hatch, poof, respawn beam… | | **arcane** | 12 | arcane beam, arcane missiles, arcane orb, blink in, blink out, magic circle cast… | | **holy** | 10 | blessing, divine shield, feather burst, halo, heal, healing ring… | | **shadow** | 12 | black hole, curse, dark explosion, eclipse, grasping hands, hex sigil… | | **status** | 13 | bleeding, burning, charmed, confused, cursed, frozen… | | **nature** | 13 | acid splash, boulder, earth spike, healing bloom, leaf storm, poison cloud… | | **weather** | 12 | aurora, blizzard, cherry blossoms, clouds, falling leaves, fireflies… | | **ui** | 12 | achievement, coin collect, combo counter, confetti, countdown, crit number… | | **pickups** | 11 | chest open, coin spin, collect burst, crystal shard, gem spin, heart pickup… | | **transitions** | 10 | blinds, burn away, crt off, diamond wipe, glitch wipe, iris… | | **critters** | 12 | bat, bird, butterfly, eyeball, fish school, flying skull… | Every effect is a file in `src/fx//.js`. The [catalog](docs/CATALOG.md) lists them all. ## use one. **In a browser game** (canvas, Phaser, PixiJS, Kaplay, three.js), use the code. No dependencies. ```js import { createFrame, clearFrame, createFx, composite } from "pixelfx"; import * as frostNova from "pixelfx/fx/ice/frost-nova"; const frame = createFrame(320, 180); // your game's pixel resolution const img = new ImageData(320, 180); const fx = createFx(frostNova, { x: 160, y: 140 }); // also: flip, angle, seed, palette, light... function tick(dt) { fx.update(dt); clearFrame(frame); fx.draw(frame, "back"); // behind characters drawCharacters(); fx.draw(frame, "front"); composite(frame, img.data, backgroundColor); // color, then light added on top ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0); // scale up with image-rendering: pixelated } ``` Install from GitHub with `npm i github:patch-gg/pixelfx`, or copy `src/core` and the effects you want. **In any engine** (Godot, Unity, GameMaker, Defold, LÖVE, Bevy), use sprite sheets: ```bash node tools/render.mjs ice/frost-nova --sheet ``` That writes a transparent PNG of every frame in a grid and an Aseprite-style JSON (frame rects, durations, and `meta.pixelfx` with fps, loop, columns and the pivot). Phaser's atlas loader and the Aseprite importers for Godot and Unity read it. `node tools/sheets.mjs` exports the whole library to `sheets/`. Any effect takes a `palette` (a dark-to-bright ramp of hex colors), so a fire can burn blue and a heal can glow pink without touching its code: ```bash node tools/render.mjs fire/torch --gif --opts '{"palette": ["#102","#215","#43a","#8cf","#cff","#fff"]}' ``` ## acting.

An effect on its own looks like a sticker. What sells a hit is the body around it: the wind-up that says something is coming, the freeze on contact, the target rocking back, the recovery. So the 61 effects with a character, and the 12 moves, say what the body does and when: ```js export const act = { target: { x: 58 }, poses: [ [-0.55, GUARD], // he starts before the effect does (t = 0 is the effect's first frame) [-0.3, WIND_UP], [0, CUT, "snap"], // "snap" holds the last pose and jumps on the key [0.06, FOLLOW_THROUGH, "snap"], [0.86, GUARD], ], hits: [{ t: 0.06, stop: 0.14, shake: 0.18, amp: 2, push: 2.8, straw: 18 }], // freeze for 0.14 s on contact }; ``` **Play the whole thing**, character and target included, by swapping `createFx` for `createAct`: ```js import { createFrame, clearFrame, createAct, composite } from "pixelfx"; import * as slash from "pixelfx/fx/melee/sword-slash"; const act = createAct(slash, { x: 80, y: 140 }); function tick(dt) { act.update(dt); // holds still by itself during a freeze clearFrame(frame); act.draw(frame); // { body: false } and { target: false } leave them out composite(frame, img.data, backgroundColor); const [sx, sy] = act.shake; // throw the picture this far ctx.putImageData(img, sx, sy); } ``` **Got your own character?** Effect ids haven't changed and a sprite sheet is still the effect alone, so existing games keep working. (Effects drawn on the body paint the stock dummy, so regenerate those if you ship them.) The timing is plain data: read `slash.act`, or `meta.pixelfx.act` in a sprite sheet's JSON (`windup`, `recovery`, `hits` with `t` and `freeze`, `poses`). Start your own wind-up animation that long before the effect, and stop updating everything for `freeze` seconds at each hit. Effects drawn on the body (frost, poison, a scan line) are written against the standing character and follow him wherever he goes: each pixel of a pose knows which pixel of the standing body it came from. `node tools/act.mjs --sheet` bakes a whole act, character included, into a sprite sheet. The body is yours to use too: `skeleton(pose)` gives you every joint of a pose in 3D, to hang your own things on, and `posedParts(pose)` gives you each part drawn on its own. ## the skill. The `pixelfx` skill teaches Claude Code to find, use, export and make effects. Install it as a plugin: ``` /plugin marketplace add patch-gg/pixelfx /plugin install pixelfx@pixelfx ``` or copy `skills/pixelfx` into `~/.claude/skills/`. Then ask for what you want: - "Add a frost nova to my mage's ultimate." - "Make five takes on a coin pickup sparkle and show me the best two." - "Export the fire and explosions categories as sprite sheets for Godot." - "This hit effect feels floaty. Make it punchier." - "Give this spell a wind-up and make the enemy react to it." ## make your own. ```bash node tools/new.mjs arcane/my-spell # a working starting point (add --loop for a loop) node tools/render.mjs arcane/my-spell # records/arcane/my-spell/contact.png: look at it node tools/check.mjs arcane/my-spell # spills, seams, unseeded randomness, slow frames ``` Then go round: look at the contact sheet, fix the worst thing, render again. `--gif` and `--mp4` show the motion, `--all` shows every frame. `node tools/act.mjs arcane/my-spell` shows an act as consecutive 12 fps steps, because motion bugs don't show in samples. [docs/AUTHORING.md](docs/AUTHORING.md) has the contract, the drawing API and the quality bar. `node tools/serve.mjs` runs the gallery locally with your effects in it. ## how it works. - **Two kinds of effect, no images.** Pure effects export `draw(p, t, o)`, the frame at `t` seconds from `t` alone, so loops tile with no seam. Simulated effects export `create(o)` and step real particles, debris and lights at 120 Hz, so sparks bounce and smoke rolls the same at any frame rate. - **Two buffers.** `color` takes pixels: opaque, dithered or truly translucent. `light` takes additive glow, added on top. Hot things look hot because of the light buffer. - **Seeded everything.** Every random number comes from the effect's seed, so frame 40 is the same every time. - **Local space.** Effects draw around their own origin; the painter places, mirrors and rotates them. Directional effects face right. A 24×38 stock character stands in for status effects, auras and hits. - **A real skeleton, drawn down to pixels.** The grey dummy is neutral on purpose, so the eye goes to the move and any effect's colors read on it. He's a 3D skeleton with fixed-length bones, pelvis to spine to shoulders, rendered in a few flat tones with one clean ink line, the way Dead Cells makes its sprites. So he can twist, bend and really turn round, and depth decides what's in front. Poses hold on 12 fps steps, the way hand-drawn sprites do, while particles run at full rate. - **Same frame shape as Sprite Fusion's VFX** (`{ w, h, ox, oy, color, light }`), so both libraries can draw into one frame. ## license. MIT, code and effects. Use them in anything, commercial included. Parts are adapted from Hugo Duprez's MIT effects and from Hollow Crown's MIT source, and the Patch Pixel font in `gallery/fonts` is Patch's own and not covered: see [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). Made by [Patch](https://patch.gg).

items.readme:
Eglantine

Eglantine is a free and opensource (FOSS) Switch 2 emulator, derived from Eden, Yuzu and Sudachi - started by developer Camille LaVey. It's written in C++ with portability in mind, with builds for Windows, Linux and macOS

Compatibility | Development | Building | Download | Support | License

## Compatibility The emulator is capable of running Mario Kart World at decent/full speed depending on specs and configurations, and Splatoon Raiders at variable performances A list of supported games will be available in future. Please be patient. ## Development For development discussions, please join us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/jCCZ58VExk) If you would like to contribute, we are open to new developers and pull requests. Please ensure that your work is of a high standard and properly documented. You can also contact any of the developers on Discord or Stoat to learn more about the current state of the emulator. ## Documentation We have a user manual! See our [User Handbook](./docs/user/README.md). ## Building See the [General Build Guide](docs/Build.md) For information on provided development tooling, see the [Tools directory](./tools) ## Download You can download the latest releases from [here](https://github.com/Djihads80/Eglantine/releases). ## Support We currently do not take in any donations for the time being If you would prefer to support us in a different way, please join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/jCCZ58VExk) ## License Eglantine is licensed under the GPLv3 (or any later version). Refer to the [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/Djihads80/Eglantine/blob/nx2/LICENSE.txt) file.

换装（可选功能） 「AI 换装」需要一个后端服务，把服装真实地「穿」到人像上。后端位于 `backend/`（GoFrame v2），支持**多模型可插拔**： | 模型别名 | 模型 | 协议 | 说明 | |---|---|---|---| | `comfyui` | **Qwen-Image-Edit-2511**（优先） / MiniMax H3 | ComfyUI 本地 API | 国内可用，无需代理网络 | | `gpt-image` | **GPT Image 2**（`gpt-image-2`） | OpenAI Images | 兼容 OpenAI 协议，支持第三方中转与代理 | | `qwen` / `zhipu` / `siliconflow` … | 通义万相 / 智谱 CogView / 硅基流动 | OpenAI Images 兼容 | 按需在配置中开启 | > 三个关键点都可配置：**API Key、Base URL、模型名**。加一个国内模型只需在配置里新增一段，无需改代码。 前端 AI 试穿页右上角提供「设置中心」，支持两种使用方式： 1. **服务器预设**：继续使用后端 `config.yaml` / 环境变量中的模型配置。 2. **个人模型配置**：在当前浏览器保存协议、Base URL、API Key 和模型名，生成时随本次请求临时发送给后端。后端不把这些字段写入数据库、配置文件或业务日志。 > 浏览器本地保存适合个人设备使用。共享设备使用完毕后，请在设置中心点击「清除本地配置」。个人 Base URL 默认禁止指向 localhost、内网和保留地址，避免公开后端被用作内网请求代理。 ### 配置模型 编辑 `backend/manifest/config/config.yaml`（模板见 `config.example.yaml`）： ```yaml llm: models: gpt-image: # 前端请求用的别名 provider: openai # 协议：openai / doubao / gemini apiKey: "" # 直接填 Key，或留空用环境变量 envKey: "OPENAI_API_KEY" # 环境变量名（优先级高于 apiKey） baseURL: "https://api.openai.com/v1" # Base URL 可改（支持中转/代理） model: "gpt-image-2" # 真实模型名 doubao: # 豆包（国内可用） provider: doubao envKey: "ARK_API_KEY" baseURL: "https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/v3" model: "doubao-seedream-3-0-t2i-250415" gemini: provider: gemini envKey: "GEMINI_API_KEY" baseURL: "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta" model: "gemini-3.1-flash-image" ``` **接入任意 OpenAI 兼容的国内生图模型**（通义万相、智谱、硅基流动等），加一段即可： ```yaml qwen: # 通义万相示例 provider: openai envKey: "DASHSCOPE_API_KEY" baseURL: "https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1" model: "wanx2.1-t2i-turbo" # 本地 ComfyUI（零成本离线极速换装，支持 Qwen-Image-Edit / MiniMax H3） comfyui: provider: comfyui baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:8188" model: "qwen-image-edit-2511" workflowPath: "workflows/comfyui_qwen_image_edit_2511_api.json" ``` ### 🎨 ComfyUI 本地离线模式（推荐：零成本、免 Key、超快速度） 如果你的电脑拥有独立显卡（或局域网有运行 ComfyUI 的主机），可以完全免 Key 使用本地生图： 1. 启动本地 ComfyUI（默认 `http://127.0.0.1:8188`）； 2. 放入 `Qwen-Image-Edit-2511` 的模型与 4 步 Lightning LoRA（详见 [`backend/README.MD`](backend/README.MD)）； 3. 打开网页右上角 **设置中心**，选择「ComfyUI 本地」，点击「测试连接」成功后保存，即可享受 4 步极速离线换装体验。系统已内置双模型自适应能力，未就绪时会自动回退至 H3 方案。 ### 🚀 后端部署（优先推荐 Docker） 后端推荐使用 **Docker / Docker Compose** 部署，无需在宿主机安装 Go 编译环境，开箱即用。 #### 方式一：Docker Compose（推荐，最省心） ```bash # 1. 复制环境变量模板并填入你的 Key（如国内免翻墙的豆包 ARK_API_KEY，或 OpenAI Key） cp backend/.env.example backend/.env # 2. 一键启动后端（内置开箱即用兜底，默认监听 8000 端口） docker compose up -d # 服务启动后监听在 http://localhost:8000 ``` > 提示：若需深度定制模型或高级路由，可复制配置文件模板：`cp backend/manifest/config/config.example.yaml backend/manifest/config/config.yaml`（未复制时系统也会自动使用模板并稳定监听 8000 端口）。 #### 方式二：Docker Run 单命令运行 ```bash cd backend # 构建镜像 docker build -f manifest/docker/Dockerfile -t costume-tryon . # 运行容器（按需注入模型 Key，例如豆包或 OpenAI） docker run -d --name costume-tryon \ -p 8000:8000 \ -e ARK_API_KEY="你的豆包ArkKey" \ -e OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-你的OpenAIKey" \ costume-tryon ``` #### 方式三：无 Docker 本地运行 - **Windows 用户**：直接双击 `backend/restart.bat` 一键自动编译并启动服务。 - **命令行运行**： ```bash cd backend # 可选：复制配置文件（不复制时也会自动安全回退加载模板并监听 8000） # cp manifest/config/config.example.yaml manifest/config/config.yaml export ARK_API_KEY="你的Key" # Windows PowerShell 用 $env:ARK_API_KEY="你的Key" go run main.go # 服务稳定监听 :8000 ``` ### 🔗 前端对接后端 前端静态页面通过以下顺序识别换装后端地址（优先级从高到低）： 1. **设置中心**：用户在当前浏览器保存的「后端 API 地址」（跨源外部公网后端须使用 `HTTPS`） 2. **全局变量**：在 HTML 加载前配置 `window.AI_API_URL = "http://localhost:8000"` 3. **URL 参数**：`https://你的前端地址/?tryon=http://localhost:8000`（安全约束：为防止钓鱼窃取 API Key 与私密照片，`?tryon=` 仅允许同源或本机回环 `localhost/127.0.0.1`；外部后端须在设置中心显式保存） 4. **本地回退**：本地以 `localhost` 或 `127.0.0.1` 访问前端时，默认自动连接 `http://127.0.0.1:8000` ### 🛡️ 接口安全与资源限制（公网部署必备） 后端原生提供企业级调用鉴权与高防资源限制（详见 [`backend/DEPLOY.md`](backend/DEPLOY.md)）： 1. **接口访问鉴权**：支持 Bearer Token 校验，服务端安全保存 SHA-256 摘要与恒定时间防侧信道比对；前端设置中心支持单独保存「后端访问 Token」，不与大模型 Key 混淆。 2. **精确 CORS 白名单**：严格域名匹配，彻底杜绝跨域滥刷与盗链。 3. **频率与额度保护**：内置令牌桶限流（默认 10 次/分）与 UTC 自然日调用额度（默认 100 次/天），超限返回标准 `429` 业务码。 4. **并发控制**：全局（默认 2 并发）与单调用主体（默认 1 并发）严格锁定，模型生图不排队堆积。 5. **图片校验与前端自适应压缩**： - 仅支持 JPEG / PNG / WebP 真实图像内容探测，严格防范伪造扩展名与代码注入； - 单图上限 8 MiB、两图合计 16 MiB、长宽限制 256~8192 px、总像素严格限制在 2000 万以内（防止解压像素炸弹导致服务器 OOM）； - 前端上传照片时自适应缩放：任一边小于 256 px 时自动等比放大到合规尺寸，高清模式最长边 2048 px，并阶梯压缩（WebP 优先，质量 0.90~0.75）。 > 完整的多模型接入、生产环境 Nginx 反代与安全加固说明见 [`backend/DEPLOY.md`](backend/DEPLOY.md)。 ## 🚀 前端本地启动 本项目前端是纯静态站点，无需构建。任选一种方式运行： ```bash # 方式一：Python 内置服务器（推荐端口 3000，与后端 8000 端口独立不冲突） python3 -m http.server 3000 # 方式二：Node 简单服务器 npx serve -l 3000 . # 方式三：直接用现代浏览器打开 index.html ``` 启动后在浏览器打开 `http://localhost:3000`。若同时启动了后端，本地换装开箱即连。 ## 📁 目录结构 ``` nvzhuang/ ├── index.html # 页面结构 + 样式 + 交互逻辑（含双语字典、AI 试穿搭配台） ├── data.js # 1407 条服装数据（id / 分类 / 关键词 / 图片路径） ├── docker-compose.yml # 一键启动后端 Docker 容器编排 ├── assets/ │ ├── thumbs/ # 缩略图（webp，网格卡片用） │ └── img/ # 展示图（webp，弹窗放大用） ├── docs/ # 文档图片、换装效果演示与姿势生图联动图 ├── backend/ # AI 换装后端（GoFrame v2，可选） │ ├── docker-compose.yml # 后端 Docker Compose 配置 │ ├── .env.example # 环境变量示例文件 │ ├── restart.bat / build.bat # Windows 本地一键启动/重新编译脚本 │ ├── manifest/config/config.yaml # 模型配置（Key / BaseURL / 模型名） │ ├── internal/logic/tryon/ # 模型适配器（openai / doubao / gemini） │ └── DEPLOY.md # 部署指南 └── .gitignore ``` > 注：原尺寸 PNG（约 1GB+）未纳入仓库，「下载原尺寸」按钮指向原站资源。 ## 🔗 URL 参数 支持通过 URL 参数直接分享特定状态： ``` ?lang=en # 初始语言（zh 为中文，en 为英文，默认 zh） ?q=lace # 初始搜索词 ?lang=en&q=white # 组合使用 ``` ## 💡 灵感来源与推荐项目 - **兄弟项目 / 姿势与生图工坊**：[拍片哥 AI 姿势参考库 (ai-pose-gallery-zh)](https://github.com/paipiange/ai-pose-gallery-zh) —— 288 组 / 1439 张多角度人体姿势，集成本地与多云端 AI 姿势生图与试穿工坊。 - **原作者 / 灵感来源**：[X @giaaibusi](https://x.com/giaaibusi) —— 诚挚鸣谢原作者对高质量 AI 服装图集的整理与创意分享！ - **社区友链**：[LINUX DO (https://linux.do/)](https://linux.do/) —— 真诚、友善、团结、专业的开源与技术极客社区。 - **审计与规范文档**： - [项目现状与开源合规审计报告 (LINUXDO_RELEASE_AUDIT.md)](docs/LINUXDO_RELEASE_AUDIT.md) - [图库内容合规与社区发布审查报告 (CONTENT_REVIEW.md)](docs/CONTENT_REVIEW.md) - [Linux.do 推广发布前核验清单 (LINUXDO_PUBLISH_CHECKLIST.md)](docs/LINUXDO_PUBLISH_CHECKLIST.md) ## 📄 开源许可证与使用规范 本项目基于 **[MIT License](LICENSE)** 协议完全免费开源，允许无限制商业使用： - **开源协议**：[MIT License](LICENSE)，代码与资产完全免费开源，允许商业使用、自由修改、集成与分发。 - **商用与创作自由**：可完全免费用于各类个人与商业作品创作（如电商广告、服装设计参考、游戏资产、AI 图像与虚拟换装应用）。 - **生成属性声明**：所有图像均为 AI 生成（t2i）概念服装设计，非现实品牌商品照片。 ## 📝 数据说明 数据存于 `data.js`，每条记录包含： | 字段 | 说明 | |---|---| | `id` | 编号（如 `SPR-0001`） | | `カテゴリ` | 分类（日文分类名，如「春」） | | `キーワード` | 关键词（英文，空格分隔） | | `サムネ` | 缩略图路径 | | `画像` | 展示图路径 | | `原寸` | 原尺寸 PNG 路径 | > 说明：`カテゴリ`、`キーワード`、`サムネ`、`画像`、`原寸` 是数据原始的日文字段名，为保持与原站数据兼容而保留。网站会在前端自动将它们本地化为中文或英文展示。 ### Data Fields (English) Each record in `data.js` contains the following fields: | Field | Description | |---|---| | `id` | Identifier (e.g. `SPR-0001`) | | `カテゴリ` | Category (Japanese category name, e.g. "春" for Spring) | | `キーワード` | Keywords (English, space-separated) | | `サムネ` | Thumbnail image path | | `画像` | Display image path | | `原寸` | Full-size PNG path | > Note: `カテゴリ`, `キーワード`, `サムネ`, `画像`, and `原寸` are the original Japanese field names kept for compatibility with the source data. The site localizes them to Chinese or English on the frontend automatically. ## Star History

# Floorplan **See how your app actually fits together.** Claude or Codex reads your codebase and draws an interactive map of it. Every part, file and web request gets a plain-English name, and every connection between them is shown. [![Claude Code plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Code-plugin-D97757?style=flat-square)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) [![Codex plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Codex-plugin-111?style=flat-square)](docs/codex.md) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/haydenschmitty/floorplan/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests)](https://github.com/haydenschmitty/floorplan/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.6.1-111?style=flat-square)](CHANGELOG.md) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-111?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Node 18+](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A518-111?style=flat-square)](https://nodejs.org) [![Zero dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-111?style=flat-square)](#how-it-works) **[Try the live demo](https://haydenschmitty.github.io/floorplan-demo/)** · [Watch the video](https://youtu.be/NTUUzC7L_NQ) · [Install](#install) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Compared](#floorplan-archify-or-understand-anything) · [Features](#features) · [See it in action](#see-it-in-action) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Docs](docs/README.md) · [FAQ](#faq)

▶ Watch the walkthrough: installing Floorplan, then a tour of Brewline, a demo coffee-subscription app built across four repos.

Try the live demo → Explore the Brewline map in your browser, no install needed.

## Why Floorplan? You built an app, probably with a lot of help from AI, and it works. But ask "what happens when someone checks out?" or "what breaks if I change this?" and the honest answer is *no idea*. Floorplan gives you the diagram nobody drew. Ask Claude Code or Codex for a floorplan and a few minutes later you have a map you can explore, ask questions on, and keep up to date as you work. - **For builders:** understand the app you made, in your own words, without reading the code. - **For teams:** onboard someone in minutes, from the big picture down to the exact file. - **For working with AI:** after every change Claude or Codex makes, see exactly which parts it touched and why. ## Floorplan, Archify or Understand Anything? All three turn code into something you can see, and all three are worth knowing. They answer different questions: | | **Floorplan** | **[Archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)** | **[Understand Anything](https://github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything)** | |---|---|---|---| | **The question it answers** | How does the app I built actually work, and what should I worry about? | How do I show this clearly? | How does this big codebase work, down to the functions? | | **Made for** | People who build with AI and don't read the code | Anyone explaining a system, a process or an idea | Developers getting to know a large codebase | | **What you get** | A zoomable map of your whole app: parts, files and endpoints, the screens, the requests between frontend and backend (even across repos), and outside services | A polished diagram in one of 10 types (architecture, sequence, ERD…) or a one-page explainer, from a repo or just a description | A knowledge graph of every file, function and class, with layers, a business-domain view and guided tours | | **Only here** | **Health check** (keys in code, open Supabase tables and Firebase rules, fakeable Stripe webhooks, endpoints anyone can use), **Recent work** (what your AI just changed, and why), blueprints from a PRD | 10 diagram types, image and video exports, diagrams of things that aren't code | Diff impact, a dashboard that adapts to your role, knowledge-base graphs | | **Runs in** | Claude Code, Codex | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and more | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and more | **Pick Floorplan** to understand and check an app you own. **Pick Archify** to draw a diagram for a doc, a talk or a decision. **Pick Understand Anything** to study a large codebase function by function. They also work together: map your app with Floorplan, then use Archify to draw one flow for a presentation. ## Features
**🗺️ A map at every zoom**
Start with the whole app, then double-click into a part, a group of files, a file, and its endpoints. Each view shows what it's used by and what it uses. 		**💬 Plain English everywhere**
"Takes card payments at checkout", not "Stripe API wrapper". Technical terms are explained on hover, and one switch shows the developer view.
**🔌 Real connections, across repos**
It follows imports, and matches each web request in your frontend to the server endpoint that answers it, even across separate repos. 		**🖥️ Start from a screen**
Pick a page you know and see everything behind it: its parts, the requests it makes, the server code, the data, and outside services.
**🧭 Ask the map**
"How does a refund reach the customer's card?" comes back as an answer plus a mini-map of just the pieces involved, with a step-by-step walkthrough. 		**🩺 Health check**
Catches the classic mistakes in AI-built apps: keys in the code or sent to the browser, Supabase tables anyone can read, open Firebase rules, Stripe webhooks anyone could fake, and endpoints with no sign-in. Each comes with a ready-to-paste fix. A check, not an audit.
**🟢 Recent work**
The cards your AI just changed light up green, each with a note on how the change serves what you asked for. 		**⚡ Stays current, stays yours**
Updates re-read only what changed, and an open map reloads itself. Everything runs on your machine, and nothing is committed to git.
Plus guided **flows** you can request in plain words, a one-minute **Start here** tour, **Export** to send a copy to anyone as one HTML file, a layout for **phones and tablets** with drag and pinch, search, keyboard shortcuts, and right-click actions on every card. ### Also: blueprints, for apps you haven't built yet Floorplan is made for mapping code you already have. It can also start from a PRD, a spec or a description of something you want to build, and draw a **blueprint**: the same kind of map, showing every part, file, endpoint and screen you'd need and how they'd fit together. Cards are dashed to show it's a plan. Instead of a Health check you get a review of what the plan still leaves open, each part has a ready request to build it, and you can reshape the plan from the map ("also plan out refunds"). Once the code exists, the blueprint becomes a map of the real thing. See [Plan something you haven't built yet](docs/getting-started.md#plan-something-you-havent-built-yet). ## See it in action Want to click around yourself? Open the [live demo](https://haydenschmitty.github.io/floorplan-demo/): the real Brewline map beside a scripted conversation, in Claude Code or Codex.

Ask the map. A real answer, from the Claude Code CLI in 31 seconds. It traced the gift from form to inbox across two repos, and spotted two bugs along the way.

Start from a screen. Pick any page and see everything behind it, from the button down to the database and outside services.

Recent work. What you asked for, what changed, and why each change was needed, on one board.

Health check. A password left in the code and an endpoint anyone can call, each with a one-click fix prompt.

Zoom in. Inside any part: what's in it, what uses it, and what it relies on. Green tags mark what just changed.

Guided flows. Watch a request travel through the app step by step, or ask for a new one to be traced.
## Install You need [Node.js 18+](https://nodejs.org) and either Claude Code or Codex. Floorplan runs on the plan you already have, with no API keys. ### Claude Code In the desktop app's Code tab or the CLI: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add haydenschmitty/floorplan claude plugin install floorplan@floorplan ``` Start a new session and it's ready. Installing the Claude Code CLI is recommended even if you use the desktop app, because it lets the map's Ask bar read your real code. More in [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md). ### Codex Signed in with ChatGPT. No terminal needed: 1. In the Codex app, open **Plugins** and choose **Add a marketplace**. 2. For **Source**, enter `haydenschmitty/floorplan` and click **Add marketplace**. 3. Find **Floorplan** and click **+** to install it. Or, from a terminal: ```bash codex plugin marketplace add haydenschmitty/floorplan codex plugin add floorplan@floorplan ``` Start a new chat and ask for a floorplan, or type `$floorplan`. The map's Ask bar runs on your own Codex sign-in, with no API key. More in [Floorplan in Codex](docs/codex.md). ## Quick start 1. Open your project in Claude Code or Codex. For a frontend and backend in separate repos, open the folder that holds both. 2. Ask: > Make me a floorplan of this app. (In Codex you can also type `$floorplan`.) 3. Explore. The map opens on its own, starting with a short tour. When you've done more work, ask: > Update the floorplan. Only what changed is re-read, and what you just worked on lights up under **Recent work**. **No code yet?** Floorplan can plan an app from a PRD or spec instead. Share the document and ask: > Here's my PRD. Make me a floorplan of what we'd need to build. You get a [blueprint](#also-blueprints-for-apps-you-havent-built-yet) of the planned system, clearly marked as a plan. ### Things to try | Ask Claude Code or Codex | Ask the map | |---|---| | "Make me a floorplan of this app" | "What happens when someone places an order?" | | "Update the floorplan" | "Where do we talk to Stripe?" | | "Fix the important issues from the floorplan's Health check" | "If I change the users table, what breaks?" | | "Add a flow showing how a new user signs up" | "Which files handle login?" | | "Rewrite the floorplan for developers" | "What did we change for refunds?" | | "Export the floorplan so I can send it to the team" | | ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR code["Your codebase
one repo or several"] --> scan["Scan
files, imports, routes, requests"] scan --> agent["Claude or Codex
names the parts, describes every file"] agent --> build["Build
map, health, screens, recent work"] build --> map["floorplan/index.html
opens in your browser"] map -. "update the floorplan" .-> scan ``` Scripts do the mechanical work: finding repos, parsing code in a dozen languages, matching web requests to endpoints, laying out the map. They're plain Node with no dependencies. Claude or Codex does the part only a reader can: deciding what the parts of your app *are*, and saying so plainly. Details in [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md). **Languages:** TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, Scala, plus Vue, Svelte and Astro files, with lighter support for others.
**Endpoints:** Express, Koa, Hono, Next.js, Firebase Cloud Functions, Flask, FastAPI, Django, Go's net/http, Gin, Echo and chi, Actix, Axum, Spring.
**Screens:** Next.js, React Router, Vue, SvelteKit, Remix, Nuxt, Astro, Expo, Angular, TanStack. ## What it adds to your project A `floorplan/` folder holding the map. In Claude Code, if you say yes, it also adds a short section to `CLAUDE.local.md` so future sessions know the map is there. **Neither is committed:** the folder ignores itself in git, and `CLAUDE.local.md` goes in your clone's private ignore list. In Codex, only the `floorplan/` folder is added. Your `.gitignore` and other tracked files are never touched. See [What's in your project](docs/project-files.md). ## Privacy - The scan, the map and its small local server all run on your computer. The server only accepts connections from your own machine. - No dependencies or install scripts, and the map works offline: its layout engine and fonts are built in. - Questions on the map go to your own account, through the Claude Code CLI or Codex, which can read your code but not change it. - The Health check never stores or shows secret values, only where they are. - No analytics or tracking. The map may ask once whether you'd like an email when Floorplan Cloud launches. Nothing is sent unless you sign up, and then only your email and "just me" or "with my team". More in [Privacy and security](docs/privacy-and-security.md). Wondering whether a plugin is safe to install? [Is it safe to install?](docs/is-it-safe.md) lists everything Floorplan does on your computer, how a test checks that on every change, and how to verify your copy. ## Documentation | | | |---|---| | [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) | Install, first map, updating, planning from a PRD, removing | | [Floorplan in Codex](docs/codex.md) | Installing and using it in Codex | | [Using the map](docs/using-the-map.md) | Every button, view, shortcut and menu | | [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md) | The pipeline, connection matching, refreshes | | [What's in your project](docs/project-files.md) | Every file Floorplan creates, and how to edit it | | [Privacy and security](docs/privacy-and-security.md) | What runs where, and what leaves your machine | | [Is it safe to install?](docs/is-it-safe.md) | No hooks, MCP servers, dependencies or downloads; every program it runs; checking your installed copy | | [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Common problems and fixes | | [Developing Floorplan](docs/development.md) | Repo layout, local installs, releases | ## FAQ
Is it safe to install? Floorplan has no hooks, no MCP servers and no dependencies, downloads nothing, and never runs code from the internet. Its only outside request is the opt-in waitlist. A test checks all of that on every change, and every release lists a fingerprint of each file so you can confirm your installed copy is the real thing. Everything is in [Is it safe to install?](docs/is-it-safe.md).
Does my code leave my computer? Only the way Claude Code and Codex always work: the AI reads the files it needs to describe your app, through your own account. The map itself is a local file and its server only listens on your machine. If you choose to open the map in the Claude app instead, Claude uploads the map (names, descriptions and structure, not your source code) to your private claude.ai account, and asks first. The one thing Floorplan itself ever sends is your email, and only if you sign up for the [Floorplan Cloud waitlist](docs/privacy-and-security.md#floorplan-cloud-waitlist).
How long does it take, and what does it cost? A first map takes a few minutes for a small app and longer for a big one, because every file and endpoint gets described. It uses your Claude or ChatGPT plan like any other task. Big projects are split across parallel helpers. Updates re-read only what changed, so they're quick and cheap.
Do I need a CLI for the Ask bar? No. The map works without one. The Ask bar answers through the Claude Code CLI or Codex, which can read your real code. Codex's desktop app already includes what it needs. With Claude, without the CLI you can ask from the Claude app instead, using the map alone.
Will it change or commit my files? It only writes its own `floorplan/` folder (and, in Claude Code if you say yes, a section in `CLAUDE.local.md`), and neither is committed. It never changes your code, your `.gitignore` or your `CLAUDE.md`.
The names it picked aren't how we talk about it. Can I change them? Yes. Just ask ("rename 'Main server' to 'Shop API' on the floorplan"), or edit `floorplan/architecture.json` and `floorplan/descriptions/` yourself. Your edits are kept on every update.
Does it work with Codex as well as Claude Code? Yes. It's the same plugin, the same map and the same Health check. Each app runs it on your own plan: Claude Code on your Claude account, Codex on your ChatGPT sign-in. A map made in one opens fine with the other. See [Floorplan in Codex](docs/codex.md).
Can I use it before I've written any code? Yes, though mapping existing code is what it's mainly for. Share a PRD, a spec or a description of your app and ask for a floorplan, and you get a blueprint: a map of what you'd need to build, marked as a plan, with a review of the decisions still open. You can change it from the map, then switch to a map of the real code once it's built. See [Plan something you haven't built yet](docs/getting-started.md#plan-something-you-havent-built-yet).
Does it work on monorepos and multi-repo setups? Yes. Point it at a monorepo, a subfolder of one, or a plain folder that holds several repos side by side. It finds every repo and connects them.
How is this different from Archify or Understand Anything? Archify draws diagrams of anything, and Understand Anything builds a developer's knowledge graph of a codebase. Floorplan maps the app you built, in plain English, and tells you what's risky and what your AI just changed. See [Floorplan, Archify or Understand Anything?](#floorplan-archify-or-understand-anything)

items.readme:
Craft Anything

English · 日本語 · 简体中文

See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust.
Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools,
has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it.

Download Craft Anything · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

How it works · Two ways to use it · AI · Agents · Under the hood · Get started · Status · Downloads · Discord


🔍 Study anything

Websites, desktop apps, phone apps, games and files: real inspection tools find out how they're built and what they do, with the evidence behind every answer.

🛠️ Build your own

Say what you want ("Recreate this website", "Recreate this game's gameplay in Rust") and a coding agent builds a new project in the stack you ask for.

✅ Checked, not guessed

Every build is compared with the original (pages at three screen widths, a game's own self-test, an app's runs) and refined until it's close.

🤖 Agent-ready

314 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool, so any agent can drive the same engine the app uses. No AI is needed to inspect.

## How it works Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps, asking you in plain words when a decision is yours: 1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs. 2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your request names (or a sensible default). 3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet. 4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
## Two ways to use it - **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it, press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom. "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode). - **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C, disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console. Both modes drive the same engine. ## Clean room or Deep - **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened) and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused and say how to turn on Deep mode. - **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start page watched, and the builder may use all of them. Switch in the title bar or Settings, with `settings_set deep_mode true`, or for one CLI run with `--deep` (or `--clean-room`).


Advanced: functions, pseudo-C, the agent and the evidence behind every answer.

## AI Building needs a coding agent on your computer. **Claude Code** is supported first: Craft Anything runs your own, unmodified `claude` program, which uses your own sign-in; Craft Anything never sees or handles your account. Your use of it falls under your own agreement with Anthropic. See [docs/claude-code.md](docs/claude-code.md) for how and why. A Codex adapter exists but hasn't been verified on a real install yet. Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter and local OpenAI-compatible servers are available for questions and analysis (Settings → AI). ## Built for agents Every tool is also a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool, so an agent can study a target or run a whole rebuild without the app: ```sh craft-anything-cli commands # every tool, by toolset craft-anything-cli mcp # serve them to any MCP client craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" ``` Results are evidence records with their confidence, coverage and limitations; big ones come back as a summary first and are paged with `core_evidence_browse`. `craft-anything-cli setup` connects Craft Anything to coding-agent apps. ## Under the hood A pure-Rust reverse-engineering engine with 314 tools (298 in the engine, the rest from the AI and setup layers) for native programs, .NET, Java, Android, Apple, Electron/JavaScript, websites, firmware, packet captures, databases and game files. Its own decoders, disassembler and decompiler work without any outside program; Deep mode uses them all, and Ghidra when it's installed. It powers the desktop app (egui), the CLI and the MCP server, and parts of it run in the browser as WebAssembly. The full list is in [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md). ## Get started Requires Rust **1.97 or newer** (a dependency needs it; `rustup update`). On Debian or Ubuntu, the desktop app also needs: ```sh sudo apt-get install libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libgtk-3-dev ``` Then: ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything && cd craft-anything cargo run --release -p craft-anything # the desktop app cargo install --path apps/craft-anything-cli # the CLI, as `craft-anything-cli` craft-anything-cli doctor # checks the install, coding agents and engines ``` Building needs a coding agent signed in on your computer (see [AI](#ai)); `doctor` says what's missing. Rebuild from the command line (questions are asked in the terminal): ```sh craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "A snake game in Rust" --rounds 1 craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Make the header blue" --continue-in "" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "Add a contact form" --project-folder "" --existing edit ``` New projects go in `Documents/Craft Anything` (change it in Settings → General). Each project folder holds `craft.json` (the request, target, status and history), `capture/` (what was recorded from the target), `app/` (the generated project), `checks/` (each comparison against the original), `investigation.cany/` (evidence) and `inbox/` (open questions). A project can also start in a folder you pick (Choose a folder… under Start, or `--project-folder`). If it already has files, you say what they are: the app itself, which the builder edits in place, or material to start from, with the app built in `app/` beside them (Settings → General can remember the answer). Settings → General also lists projects from more folders; removing one only takes it off the list. ## Status > [!IMPORTANT] > **Status:** Craft Anything is in early alpha. What works today, what is partial and what's next: > > - **Works today:** the desktop app (Simple and Advanced), the CLI and the MCP server; the > Study → Build → Check → Refine workflow for websites, apps and games with Claude Code as the > builder; website checks at three screen widths; game rebuilds in Unity, Unreal or Godot; Deep > mode with Ghidra; generated pictures and 3D models (opt-in, your own fal.ai key); plugins (MCP > servers, and WASM components in builds with the `wasm-plugins` option). > - **Partly there:** building with API keys and other coding agents (built, not yet run live), > behaviour checks for apps and games, a few engine tools tested only against stand-ins. > - **Next:** the first public release (installers for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD, and the > browser viewer are set up in CI), then the managed tier. > > [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) has the detail and how each part was checked, > [docs/tool-status.md](docs/tool-status.md) the tool-by-tool checklist, and > [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) the plan, item by item. Please file issues, or tell us what > broke on [Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft). **Responsible use.** Use Craft Anything on software you own or are allowed to examine. It never bypasses DRM, logins or anti-cheat. Rebuilds recreate layout, style and behaviour from evidence; the agent is told not to copy logos, photos or text unless you confirm you own them or have permission. ## Downloads On GitHub, the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/latest) has every build listed below, and [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases) has earlier versions and their notes. `` in the file names is the version number, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for every file. ### Windows | Build | Installer | Portable | |---|---|---| | x64 (64-bit Intel/AMD) | `craft-anything--windows-x64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x64-portable.zip` | | arm64 (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs) | `craft-anything--windows-arm64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-arm64-portable.zip` | | x86 (32-bit) | `craft-anything--windows-x86.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x86-portable.zip` | Installers and executables are code-signed. The portable zip keeps its settings next to the app. ### macOS | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | App, universal (Apple silicon + Intel) | `craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg` | Signed and notarized | | Command-line tool, universal | `craft-anything-cli--macos-universal.zip` | Signed and notarized; see below if macOS blocks it | Versions after 0.2.0 include the command-line tool in the app, so builds don't need the separate zip. You only need it to use the command line without the app. A browser download of the zip can stop with "Apple could not verify craft-anything-cli" (a lone program can't carry its notarization with it, so macOS has to look it up online). A download from the terminal isn't checked this way, so use this instead: ```sh ver=0.2.0 # change this to the version you want curl -fLO "https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/download/v$ver/craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" ditto -x -k "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" . mkdir -p ~/.local/bin mv "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal/craft-anything-cli" ~/.local/bin/ ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli --version ``` To run it as just `craft-anything-cli`, add `~/.local/bin` to your `PATH`. If you already have the blocked copy, press Done (not Move to Bin), then run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine `, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. ### Linux | Format | x86_64 | aarch64 (ARM64) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | AppImage | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.AppImage` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.AppImage` | Runs anywhere; updates itself with [AppImageUpdate](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/AppImageUpdate) (`.zsync` files) | | Flatpak | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.flatpak` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.flatpak` | Sandboxed; `flatpak install --user ` | | Debian/Ubuntu | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.deb` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.deb` | | | Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.rpm` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.rpm` | | | Tarball | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Unpack anywhere | RISC-V (riscv64): `craft-anything--linux-riscv64.tar.gz`, a tarball only. ### FreeBSD | Build | File | |---|---| | x86_64 | `craft-anything--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | ### Web (WebAssembly) | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | Browser viewer | `craft-anything-web-.zip` | Says what a file is, in the browser (the file never leaves it); host the folder on any static web server ([packaging/web/README.md](packaging/web/README.md)) |
