items.description: Say cheese! Star this repo and your profile picture gets printed out on a receipt printer.
items.readme: # print-my-profile-pic Star this repo to have your GitHub profile picture framed, printed out on my receipt printer, and stuck to my wall. That's it! > [!TIP] > If you give a one-time [sponsorship](https://github.com/sponsors/aschmelyun?frequency=one-time&sponsor=aschmelyun) of any amount beforehand, your profile picture will be printed in a **special frame**. ## How's it work? GitHub allows you to create webhooks for specific events on your repos, I've set one up for [starring](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#star) this project. When that happens, a payload is POSTed to a [Cloudflare tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/) domain, which leads to a PHP script running on a Raspberry Pi that's sitting on my desk. From the inbound request, you can gleen info about the person who starred the repo, like their display name and avatar URL. The script takes their profile picture, renders it behind a cut-out of a photo frame, and then adds some other info I thought should be included in each receipt. The RPi is connected to an Epson TM-T88IV thermal receipt printer via USB, and the PHP script uses my go-to [escpos-php](https://github.com/mike42/escpos-php) library to format the receipt data and send it off to the printer. ## But why? It sounded fun when my friend [Sam](https://x.com/samwhoo) mentioned it. That's pretty much it! ## What now? I'll periodically update this README with a picture of the pinboard I've dubbed the "Hall of Frame" as pictures get added to it. Want to add a new frame? Send in a PR!

items.title: lexifina/global-law
items.description: Git for Global Law: the law of every country as one git history, each country's record a submodule, every commit one law taking effect
items.readme:
# Git for Global Law

**The world's law in one git history. Every word traced to the law that wrote it for any country and any date.**

An expansion of the same for the US Code, [#1 on Hacker News (28/10/26)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50268380).
Semantic, searchable law on a global scale.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f24f3411-24d9-416a-8c45-9cebc817c64e

**Free to use: [CC0](LICENSE.md).** Fork it, build on it, ship it in a product: no permission or credit needed. The law text
sits in each country's repository, under that repository's own terms.

The law of many jurisdictions as one git history. Each jurisdiction's law is its own repository, where every commit
is one law taking effect, written by that law. This repository arranges those repositories by jurisdiction and
interleaves their histories in the order the changes took force, so a single commit here is the state of all of them on
one day.

```
global-law/
├── manifest.json            every corpus: path, source repo, coverage, which trailer holds the in-force date
├── jurisdiction.json        the world, and its children: 193 UN members, other territories with their own ISO code, and the EU
├── germany/                 Germany (ISO code DE in its jurisdiction.json)
│   ├── SOURCES.md           where German law can be read, with what each source offers
│   └── bund/                federal law
│       └── acts/            submodule: the Grundgesetz since 1949 (grundgesetz/), every other federal act since 2019
├── estonia/                 Estonia
│   └── national/acts/       submodule: Estonia's law history, from its corpus.json
├── france/                  France: jurisdiction.json and SOURCES.md, no history yet
└── …                        every other country, the same way
```

Each country's law lives in its own repository, `lexifina/<country>-law`, which says where it belongs here in a
`corpus.json` at its root. A country whose repository still holds only its sources (no law yet) has a folder with its
`jurisdiction.json` and `SOURCES.md`, and no submodule: only real law is pinned. Laws adopted but not yet in force stay
on each corpus's future branch; `main` here holds only what is in force by the build date.

Corpora differ widely in reach. Some hold a country's whole statute book (Czechia, Spain, Switzerland, Georgia, Malta);
others hold a few acts, or a sample: the US corpus is nine titles of the United States Code, and the UK corpus is the
special educational needs law. `manifest.json` gives each corpus's `coverage`, and `history` says how its past is known:
`in-force` (dated official versions), `replayed` (rebuilt by applying each amending act; its `verification` says which
dates were checked) or `current-only` (today's text only).

## Using it from an AI model (MCP)

`tools/mcp_server.py` is a Model Context Protocol server for this tree. It lets Claude or any other MCP client ask the
law what it said on a date, and every answer states where its record starts and ends. It uses only Python 3.10+ and
git, runs on your machine over stdio, reads the repository and changes nothing. It makes no network calls.

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/lexifina/global-law && cd global-law
claude mcp add global-law -- python tools/mcp_server.py      # Claude Code; or approve the project's .mcp.json
```

For other clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor and the like), add this to their MCP settings:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "global-law": { "command": "python", "args": ["/path/to/global-law/tools/mcp_server.py"] } } }
```

Then ask in plain words, for example:

- "What did 11 U.S.C. §1182(1) say on 1 May 2022, and which law last changed it?"
- "A case was commenced on 2022-05-01 under §1182. Which text applies, period by period?"
- "Is the text of s. 42 Children and Families Act 2014 that the Court of Appeal applied in 2020 still in force?"
- "Which provisions rely on 11 U.S.C. §1182, and which judgments does the record hold for it?"
- "Check every citation in this brief against the law in force today."

It has 18 read-only tools, three prompts and a resource template. The tools cover finding a provision, reading it on a
date, who wrote each word, comparing dates, a provision's history, the laws between two dates, searching the text and
the change notes, when words entered or left the law, what else a change affects, checking precedent, resolving the
citations in a brief, and which text applies to a case. Old paths with ISO country codes (`us/federal/usc/...`, `de`)
are still read. MCP.md has the full tool list, the protocol versions, the security measures and how it compares with
other law MCP servers. The tests are `python -m unittest tests.test_mcp`.

## How it is built

- The first commit, dated 1 January 1970, holds the jurisdiction tree and the list of corpora, and no law.
- Every later commit moves exactly one corpus to its next commit. Its author is the law, as in the corpus, and its
  trailers name the corpus, the corpus commit, the law and the in-force date.
- The order is the in-force date, keeping each corpus's own order.
- The last commit adds this README, the tools and the tests.
- The build is deterministic. When a corpus is rebuilt, for example after a correction, this repository is rebuilt from
  scratch and force-pushed.

## Dates

Git cannot store dates before 1970, so changes to the Grundgesetz that took effect earlier carry 1970 commit dates, one
second apart, in the right order. The `In-force` trailer is authoritative and the tools use it, so
`law.py show 1956-03-19 …` works.

## What it does not show

- Each corpus covers only what its README says. A file missing on a date can mean the provision was not yet in force or
  that the corpus does not reach that far back.
- A later law that reaches back to earlier dates (retroactive application) is recorded in the corpus's commit messages
  but does not change the text shown on those earlier dates.
- `git blame` works by line, so a line changed in part is credited to the last law that touched it. `law.py words`
  credits each word instead, by comparing each version with the one before; text rewritten in place is credited to
  the law that rewrote it, even where a few of its words are the same as before.

## Visualisation suite

![How long each country's law waits between adoption and entry into force, one distribution per jurisdiction](visualisations/the-shape-of-waiting.png)

[See all global law cohort visualisations and bridges here](visualisations/)

## Reading it

```
git clone https://github.com/lexifina/global-law && cd global-law
git submodule update --init

python tools/law.py world 2022-05-01                       what every corpus looked like that day
python tools/law.py show 2022-05-01 united-states/federal/usc/title-11/1182.md
python tools/law.py blame 2022-07-01 united-states/federal/usc/title-11/1182.md
python tools/law.py words 2022-07-01 united-states/federal/usc/title-11/1182.md
python tools/law.py diff 2022-05-01 2022-07-01 united-states/federal/usc/title-11/1182.md
python tools/law.py laws 1990-01-01 1990-12-31 germany
```

Dates must be written YYYY-MM-DD. When a date falls before a record starts or after it ends, the tools say so on
stderr, because each country's record covers a different period (see `record_to` in `manifest.json`).

Plain git works too, with care:

- `git log --first-parent` is a world chronology of laws taking effect.
- `git grep --recurse-submodules <term> <commit>` searches all the law in force at that moment, in every country.
- `git diff --submodule=diff <commit> <commit>` shows every change in every country between two moments.
- Inside a corpus, `git blame` names the law that wrote each line, and `git log -p --word-diff -- <file>` shows each
  law's change word by word, which matters where a line is a whole paragraph. Blame and log do not cross from here
  into a corpus: run them in the corpus folder, or use `law.py`.
- To look around an older moment, use a separate worktree, not `git checkout` here:
  `git worktree add ../then <commit> && cd ../then && git submodule update --init`. Checking out an old commit here
  leaves the folders of corpora that did not exist yet, and the tools, which live in the last commit, disappear.
- Git cannot store dates before 1970, so `git log --before=1960-01-01` gives a wrong answer without saying so. The
  tools read the `In-force` trailer instead.
- Each corpus's own tags are copied here under its path, for example `germany/bund/acts/gg/36`.
- After a corpus is rebuilt (its maintainers force-push), run `git submodule update --init` and, inside that corpus,
  `git fetch --force --tags`: a plain fetch keeps old tags with the same names.

records the command, the software, the commits pinned, the decisions made by hand and what an AI model did and did

# Tongjiang Lab

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**Free, interactive 3D science lessons for high school — physics, chemistry, biology and geography.**

Try them online: **https://lab.tongjiang.app**

There are 54 lessons so far. Each one is a **single self-contained HTML file** of about 1 MB: double-click to open it, and it works offline, on a projector or on an interactive whiteboard. Every lesson is one 3D world with a live control console, a guiding question and a step-by-step path a teacher can follow from start to finish.

The lessons follow the Chinese national curriculum standards for senior high school and the People's Education Press (PEP) 2019 textbooks. The lesson interface is currently in Chinese; other languages are planned.

- **Embed**: `<iframe src="https://lab.tongjiang.app/<slug>" width="100%" style="aspect-ratio:16/9;border:0" allow="fullscreen"></iframe>`

items.readme: # florilegium [![build](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/actions/workflows/build.yml) [![playground](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/actions/workflows/pages.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://kevinraymond.github.io/florilegium/) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kevinraymond/florilegium?color=2456c4)](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/releases/latest) [![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/kevinraymond/florilegium?color=2456c4)](LICENSE) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium) ## Origin The [Reddit post](https://www.reddit.com/r/LaTeX/comments/1xixznw/how_do_you_make_these_flowers_in_latex/) asked how to make flowers like these in LaTeX. I don't know how the original was made. This project is one possible way, and the way I did it uses hand-authored primitives with randomized parameters, painted in Lua and placed by a procedural layout whose "fill the unused space" part borrows a 1998 idea from the ornament literature. It gets a similar look, but I explicitly tried to not replicate the original. This project was made with the assistance of AI (Claude), and I'm sharing the [process I used](PROCESS.md) to bring it to life. ## What it is Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LaTeX. No images, no imported paths, no external assets: every petal, leaf and stem is a parametric curve computed in Lua while the page is being written, painted like a watercolor, and written straight into the PDF. Every page gets its own garden. [Try it in your browser](https://kevinraymond.github.io/florilegium/). The playground sets a page as a printer's proof, grows its margin with the same Lua, and hands it back as an SVG, a LaTeX preamble or a Typst page setup. ![six seeds](gallery/seeds.gif) *Six seeds of the grown composition. Same code, different seed — and the garden fills whatever space the text leaves free.* Two documents share one package, and two more (`showcase.tex`, `spread.tex`) show what else it does: | | `florilegium.tex` | `florilegium-grow.tex` | |---|---|---| | composition | **authored**: stems, leaves and flowers placed by hand, every parameter sampled | **grown**: a plant grown to fit the page by a greedy space-filling loop | | adapts to | nothing (tuned for A4, 68 mm margin) | the page layout, and the free space below the text on the last page | | preview | | | | PDF | [florilegium.pdf](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/releases/latest/download/florilegium.pdf) | [florilegium-grow.pdf](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/releases/latest/download/florilegium-grow.pdf) | Both PDFs are self-describing: the body text is the write-up of how the margin is drawn. ![last page of the grown document](gallery/preview-grown-lastpage.png) *Last page of the grown document: the text ends early, so branches arch into the space below.* ![detail](gallery/detail.png) *300 dpi crop. Mottled washes with white streaks lifted out, lobed leaves with white veins, forget-me-not cymes, a pale ghost flower behind the stems.* ## Watch it grow | as it grows | with the free space it fills | |---|---| | | | *Seed 6, from an empty margin to the finished page. The stems rise first, leaves open as the tips pass their nodes, and each stem ends in a flower. Then the greedy loop takes over: on the right, each dashed circle is the largest free disc it found, just before a branch grows to it. Big holes come first and slowly, small ones last and fast. The butterflies and bees fly in, the bird glides onto its twig, and the snail crawls up its stem until the last frame, which is exactly the page this seed always gives.* The growth is recorded once, while the page is laid out: each stem is also drawn as prefixes of increasing length and each motif at a few smaller scales, replaying the same random draws. A frame then writes the pieces whose time has come, in their original painting order. `make grow-6` renders one seed this way (`build/grow-6.gif` and `.mp4`, about 45 seconds); add `EXPLAIN=1` for the dashed circles. ## The margin reads the text ![the three pages of showcase.tex](gallery/preview-showcase.png) *`showcase.tex`, "A year in the margin": spring on the first page, summer, autumn on the last. Each section describes the feature it shows. Download [showcase.pdf](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/releases/latest/download/showcase.pdf).* The grown margin can respond to the document around it: - **Initials.** `\florilegiuminitial[5]{E}` sets the first letter of a paragraph in a tile five lines tall. The outline of the letter is read from an OpenType font (Latin Modern Bold by default) and painted like a petal; a vine passes over and under its strokes in turn, with leaves where they fit and flowers in the gaps, often in the letter's counters. The letter is also typeset invisibly, so the paragraph still copies as "Every". - **Flowers at the headings.** With the option `sections`, every numbered section and subsection gets a flower in the margin beside its heading, painted in the copper of the accents, the way headings were once picked out in red. - **A flower where the text asks.** `\florilegiumbloom` puts a flower beside the line it stands in; `\florilegiumbloom[lily]` asks for any motif of the garden. The marks are found in the page box when the page is shipped out, so this works in one run. - **Seasons.** With the option `aging`, the garden ages from spring on the first page (mostly in bud, small pale leaves) to autumn on the last (seed heads, falling petals, a few copper leaves). It needs two runs, for the page count; `\florilegiumage{0.8}` sets an age by hand instead. ![four initials](gallery/initials.png) ![one seed through the seasons](gallery/seasons.png) *One seed in spring, early summer, late summer and autumn. The seasons change what grows, not where.* ## Visitors ![detail with a bird and a snail](gallery/detail-visitors.png) Most pages have visitors: a butterfly or two and bees in the open spaces, a snail crawling up one of the main stems, and on about one page in five a bird perched on a twig of its own. They come from a random stream of their own, so a page without them is exactly the page it would have been; the option `novisitors` leaves them out. ## Any ink ![one seed in six inks](gallery/inks.png) *The whole palette comes from one color, `ink`: Delft blue, sepia, green, crimson, violet, teal. The ramp from the darkest stroke to the palest wash is computed from that hue in OKLCH, so the light end never turns gray.* ## Themes ![seed 6 as flora, geometric and math](gallery/themes.png) *Seed 6 three times: as it always grew, with `theme=geometric`, and with `theme=math`.* The growth loop never knew what it was drawing. It reads a table of motifs (the size of the disc each one takes, a weight, a function that draws it) and calls every primitive by name. A theme is one Lua file, `florilegium-theme-.lua`, that replaces some of those primitives and may add rows to the table, or brings a composition of its own. **`theme=geometric`** is the same plant cut from flat shapes (`florilegium-theme-geometric.lua`). It grows exactly as the flowers do, and only the drawing changes: the stems run straight between their nodes, the leaves are kites and toothed polygons folded into a light and a dark facet with straight white veins, the flowers are rosettes of rhombi or layered star polygons, the tendrils square spirals, the bird and the butterfly low-poly. The colors are flat tones of the ink, with no wash; crystals (Platonic solids, flat-shaded like cut stones) grow among the flowers. A page is about a tenth of the size of a flora page. ![the primitives of the geometric theme](gallery/specimen-geometric.png) **`theme=math`** is no plant at all (`florilegium-theme-math.lua`, drawing from `florilegium-figures.lua`): mathematics cascading down the margin and across the bottom of the page, overlapping a little so it blends. A large figure sits in the corner where the column meets the bottom (an Apollonian gasket, a deep Koch snowflake, Vogel's disc, a polyhedron). Down the column run one or two *families*, figures that change as they go, joined by small copper arrows: the Koch snowflake gaining a level, a polygon gaining sides on its way to the circle, the cube truncating into the octahedron, chords k → mk mod n turning from a cardioid into a nephroid, Vogel's disc packing evenly only at the golden angle. Equations that hold (e^{iπ} + 1 = 0, V − E + F = 2, ...) run along the bottom and under the text on the last page, and everything else, largest hole first, is figures (Platonic solids, knots, Hilbert curves, Lissajous curves, hypotrochoids, Maurer roses, the Petersen graph, ...), letters, numerals and symbols set by TeX at many sizes and a slight tilt, and dots. It fills whatever space the page leaves, like the garden; `density` sets how much there is. ```latex \usepackage[grown,theme=geometric]{florilegium} % or theme=math; the whole document \florilegiumtheme{math} % or from the page this stands on ``` A document without a theme comes out byte for byte as it did before themes existed. ## Less in the margin ![seed 6 at density 1, 0.5, 0.2 and 0.05, and at intensity 0.5](gallery/dials.png) *Seed 6 at `density=1`, `0.5`, `0.2` and `0.05`, and at `intensity=0.5`.* A full garden is a lot to have beside an equation. Two options turn it down, with any theme: - **`density=0.4`** grows less: the loop stops at larger holes, keeps more paper around each motif, and hangs fewer leaves and fillers. Low on the dial the plant itself thins out: two main stems, then one, no footer; at `0.05` it is a single vine with its flower, a couple of leaves and one or two sprays. With the math theme it means fewer things. - **`intensity=0.5`** paints the whole margin paler, the same way the ghost flowers behind the garden are painted. It changes only the color, not the detail. ```latex \usepackage[grown,density=0.4,intensity=0.6]{florilegium} ``` At the defaults (`1` and `1`) every page is exactly the page it was before. ## One ornament in the text ![\florilegiumornament](gallery/ornaments.png) Or no margin at all: `\florilegiumornament{leaf}` sets one primitive in the line, in a box the size of a letter, for example to open a paragraph. Each ornament in a document gets a shape of its own and keeps it from one build to the next; `seed=random` draws a new one every time the PDF is built, and `seed=7` a fixed one. ```latex \usepackage[nomargin]{florilegium} % ornaments only, no garden in the margin \florilegiumornament{leaf} A paragraph that opens with a leaf. \florilegiumornament[size=2.4em, ink=5B2A1F, angle=30, seed=random]{flower} ``` Any primitive works (`leaf`, `leaflet`, `flower`, `blossom`, `bud`, `bell`, `lily`, `cyme`, `umbel`, `butterfly`, `bee`, `bird`, `hedera`, `sparkle`, ...), and so do the current theme's (`crystal` with `geometric`; `knot`, `polyhedron`, `koch`, ... with `math`). ## Both sides of the page ![pages 2 and 3 of spread.tex](gallery/spread.png) *`spread.tex`, pages 2 and 3: a two-sided document with a wide outer margin. The garden grows on the left of the left-hand page and, mirrored, on the right of the right-hand page. The last page also switches to the geometric theme. Download [spread.pdf](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/releases/latest/download/spread.pdf).* The garden grows in whichever side margin is wider, so there is nothing to set. In a two-sided document (`twoside` with a wide `outer` margin) it changes sides with the page. A one-sided document with a wide right margin gets it on the right of every page. A mirrored page is laid out as if seen in a mirror, then drawn through a reflection: the last transform that every point already passes through. It is exactly the reflection of the garden the same seed would grow on the left. ## SVG, Typst and the browser ![the playground: a proof of the page on the left, its colophon on the right](gallery/playground.png) *The [playground](https://kevinraymond.github.io/florilegium/), seed 12 in autumn on a last page. The page is a proof, and its colophon, the note a book keeps about its paper, ink and printing, is the set of controls: every copper word in it can be changed.* The same Lua can draw a page without TeX. `florilegium-svg.lua` runs the package's own code with a small stand-in for the few parts of TeX it touches (the page's lengths, the page number, and the node a drawing goes into), takes the PDF drawing commands that `florilegium-ink.lua` writes as it always does, and rewrites them as SVG. Nothing in the drawing code changes, so the garden is the one LuaLaTeX would draw, not an imitation of it. ```sh texlua florilegium-svg.lua --seed 7 > margin.svg # page 1 of a document with \def\florilegiumseed{7} lua florilegium-svg.lua --seed 7 --season autumn --ink 5B2A1F --left 25mm --right 65mm > margin.svg texlua florilegium-svg.lua --help # paper, margins, two-sided pages, the last page, themes... make svg SEED=7 # -> build/svg-7.svg ``` Any Lua 5.3 or 5.4 runs it. Lengths are read the way TeX reads them and colors are converted the way xcolor converts them, so `--seed 7` with the default margins gives, byte for byte, the drawing on page 1 of `florilegium-grow.tex` built with seed 7. The SVG is a whole page with a transparent background, which makes it a page background anywhere. In Typst: ```typst #set page(paper: "a4", margin: (left: 68mm, right: 22mm, top: 32mm, bottom: 30mm), background: image("margin.svg", width: 100%, height: 100%)) ``` The playground runs the same files in the browser with [wasmoon](https://github.com/ceifa/wasmoon), Lua 5.4 compiled to WebAssembly, in a background worker, and a page grows in about a second. Seed 7 there is seed 7 here. The proof is the control surface as much as the colophon is: the measure above it sets the margin, and dragging the foot of the text up makes a last page. The text on the proof describes the garden that just grew, from the counts the growth loop keeps. Under it, the page can be seen as readers with protanopia, deuteranopia or tritanopia see it, with the distance between the ink and the accent measured for each (Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes's model, distances in Oklab); a pairing that is hard to tell apart is flagged when you choose it. Next to the download are the LaTeX preamble, the Typst setup and the command line that make the same garden, and the address bar keeps every setting, so a garden can be shared as a link. To run it from a clone, serve the repository with `make playground` and open . The math theme works too. Its figures come from the same Lua; its equations and symbols, which TeX sets in a PDF, are set in the playground by MathJax in the same Computer Modern, and the command line leaves them out. The fonts are served with the page (IM FELL DW Pica, and Latin Modern renamed as its license asks), so nothing is fetched from a font service. ## In PostScript ![the two pages of postscript/florilegium.ps, seed 7](gallery/preview-postscript.png) *`postscript/florilegium.ps`: the grown margin in pure PostScript, one self-contained file. Ghostscript, or a printer, computes every petal while it interprets the page, and the two pages of text explain how.* The drawing core, every primitive and the growth loop are ported from `florilegium-ink.lua`, `florilegium-flora.lua` and `florilegium-grow.lua`, procedure for procedure. It needs no TeX and no other file: ```sh gs -dALLOWPSTRANSPARENCY -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dSeed=7 -o garden.pdf postscript/florilegium.ps make postscript # the same -> build/postscript-7.pdf; SEED=12 for another garden ``` `-dSeed=N` picks the garden; without it the interpreter's calendar picks one, so every print is new. `-dAge=0` to `1` sets the season, and `-dNoVisitors` leaves out the butterflies, bees, snail and bird. Two pages take about 2.5 seconds. Much of the Lua maps directly: PostScript's own transformation matrix places each primitive (translate, rotate, scale), paths and Bézier curves are native, and procedures built at run time stand in for Lua's closures (a petal's half-width is a procedure handed to the outline builder). Four things don't map: - **Layers.** The garden grows in one order but is painted back to front, so every fill and stroke is captured with `pathforall` into a list per layer, and the lists are played back at the end. - **Transparency.** PostScript has none. Ghostscript provides it with `-dALLOWPSTRANSPARENCY`. Without that flag, or on a printer, each translucent fill is mixed with the color it is likely to land on and painted opaque. The result is flatter, but it's the same garden. - **Randomness.** The generator is Park-Miller in 32-bit integer arithmetic, and PostScript reals are single precision, so seed 7 here is a different garden from seed 7 in LaTeX. - **Text.** The file typesets its own two pages in Times. It knows where its headings are and where its text ends, so the copper flowers at the headings and the garden under the last line work as they do in LaTeX. It has no initials, animation, themes, mirrored pages, density or intensity, ornaments in the text, or authored composition. [`postscript/README.md`](postscript/README.md) describes every option, how a seed is chosen when none is given, what to know before porting the file further, and the tests that `postscript/check.sh` runs on it. *The file sent twice to an Epson inkjet with `lp postscript/florilegium.ps`, with no seed given. The computer's print system runs the program again for each job, so each print takes its seed from the clock and grows a different garden. A printer gets the opaque version, as it has no transparency.* ## Build LuaLaTeX, one pass, about a second a page (two passes for `showcase.tex`, whose seasons need the page count). ```sh make # the four PDFs make seed-7 # one page from seed 7 -> build/seed-7.pdf make gallery # gallery/seeds.png + seeds.gif, inks.png, seasons.png, themes.png, dials.png (python3, Pillow, pdftoppm) make grow-6 # growth animation of seed 6 -> build/grow-6.gif + .mp4 (ffmpeg) make grow-6 EXPLAIN=1 # the same with the free discs marked -> build/grow-6-explain.* make svg SEED=7 # the same page as SVG, without TeX -> build/svg-7.svg make playground # the browser playground at http://localhost:8000/web/ ``` No TeX installed? Build the image once and run everything in it: ```sh docker build -t florilegium-tex tools make RUN=tools/in-docker ``` Or paste `florilegium.sty`, the `.lua` files and one of the `.tex` files into an [Overleaf](https://www.overleaf.com) project and set the compiler to LuaLaTeX. Use it in your own document: ```latex \usepackage[grown]{florilegium} % or plain \usepackage{florilegium} for the authored one % options for the grown one: sections (flowers at the headings), aging (two runs), % novisitors (no butterflies, bees, snails or birds); for both: theme=geometric or theme=math, % density=0.4 (grown only), intensity=0.6 % two-sided? nothing to set: the garden grows in the wider side margin \definecolor{ink}{HTML}{5B2A1F} % optional: the hue of the whole palette (this is sepia) \definecolor{accent}{HTML}{B4662F} % optional: the copper of the hairlines ... \florilegiuminitial[4]{T}his paragraph starts with a decorated T. ... a flower in the margin beside this line\florilegiumbloom ... \florilegiumage{0.8} % grown only: autumn from here on \florilegiumtheme{geometric} % another theme, from the page this stands on \florilegiumornament{leaf} % one leaf in the text, the size of a letter \florilegiumtextend % grown only: at the very end of the text ``` A fixed seed instead of the page number: `lualatex "\def\florilegiumseed{7}\input{florilegium-grow.tex}"`. Any primitive can be drawn on its own inside a TikZ picture, under the current scope's shift, rotation and scale: ```latex \begin{tikzpicture} \begin{scope}[shift={(2,2)},rotate=20]\florilegiumdraw{flower}{1.3}\end{scope} \begin{scope}[shift={(5,0)}]\florilegiumdraw{leaf}{3.0, {depth=0.6}}\end{scope} \begin{scope}[shift={(8,1)}]\florilegiumdraw{ghost}{"lily", {s=1.4}}\end{scope} \begin{scope}[shift={(11,1)}]\florilegiumdraw{butterfly}{1.5}\end{scope} \end{tikzpicture} ``` With a theme, its primitives can be drawn by name too: `\florilegiumdraw{crystal}{1.0}` under `theme=geometric` (see `specimen-geometric.tex`), `\florilegiumdraw{knot}{1.2}` under `theme=math`. ## How it works **Drawing** (`florilegium-ink.lua`). All geometry is computed in Lua and written as PDF path operators into one literal node per page; TeX does no arithmetic. Primitives are drawn in a local frame under an affine transform, which is read from TikZ when a primitive is called inside a scope. Colors come from a tone ramp derived from the one document color `ink`: navy to mist at the hue of `ink`, interpolated in OKLCH so the light end stays blue instead of turning gray. Tapered strokes are two offset Béziers, not sampled ribbons. **Primitives** (`florilegium-flora.lua`). Painted in the order a watercolorist would: a flat wash, darker blotches multiplied over it, pigment pooling at the edges, streaks lifted out in white, a few fine veins, and almost no outlines. Broad petals and flowers, star lilies seen at a tilt, blossoms and florets, buds and bellflowers; lobed and entire leaves; forget-me-not cymes that curl like a scorpion's tail, branching sprigs, umbels, tendrils, seed heads; butterflies, bees, snails and a bird; copper sparkles, rosettes and the ivy-leaf fleuron whose stem becomes the head rule. Any of them can be painted as a pale ghost. **Authored composition** (`florilegium-authored.lua`). A plant grows from a root in the bottom-left corner: three stems through hand-picked control points, a fourth along the bottom of the page as the footer, leaves at chosen fractions of the stems, and every other motif on a branch that leaves its stem tangentially and arrives along the motif's axis — so every flower can be traced back to the root. **Grown composition** (`florilegium-grow.lua`), in the spirit of Wong, Zongker & Salesin, [*Computer-Generated Floral Ornament*](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/280814.280948) (SIGGRAPH 1998). The stems sway up the column as smooth noise of their height; leaves are hung at their nodes where there is room. Then, repeatedly: take the largest free disc within reach of a stem, choose a motif that fits it, and grow a branch to it from the nearest stem point; the branch becomes a stem in turn. Big holes are taken first, so flowers and lilies land early, sprays and leaves fill the middle, and the loop ends by tucking leaflets, buds and florets onto the stems. The end of the text is measured with `\pagetotal` in the same pass, so a short last page grows branches into the space below it with one compilation. **Reading the page** (`florilegium.lua`). A heading or `\florilegiumbloom` leaves an invisible marker node in the text. When the page is shipped out, its box is walked node by node, adding up heights, depths and the glue as it was set, to find each marker's height on the page; the garden then gives those lines their flowers before any leaf is hung. An age reweights the motifs: buds and sprays of buds in spring, seed heads in autumn, when some leaves are painted with a ramp built from the accent instead of the ink. **Initials** (`florilegium-initial.lua`). The letter's outline comes from luaotfload's OpenType reader as Bézier segments. Flattened into polygons, it gives an even-odd inside test, and a grid of distances to the letter and the frame finds the largest gaps for the flowers. The vine is a Catmull-Rom curve across the tile; where it crosses the letter it goes over and under in turn, and the strands that go over are drawn again, clipped to the letter, with a thin halo of paper. **Procedural ≠ random.** The seed is derived from the page number, so page *n* always gets garden *n*. Reproducibility is what makes the document stable enough to typeset. See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for a handoff-style map of the code, the tunables, and ideas not yet done. ## Credits - The [Reddit post](https://www.reddit.com/r/LaTeX/comments/1xixznw/how_do_you_make_these_flowers_in_latex/) that asked the question (see [Origin](#origin)). - The growth loop follows Wong, Zongker & Salesin, [*Computer-Generated Floral Ornament*](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/280814.280948) (SIGGRAPH 1998). - The tone ramp is computed in [Oklab](https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/), Björn Ottosson's perceptual color space; the conversion matrices in `florilegium-ink.lua` are his, released into the public domain. - The random numbers come from [mulberry32](https://gist.github.com/tommyettinger/46a874533244883189143505d203312c), Tommy Ettinger's public-domain generator. The PostScript port uses the "minimal standard" generator of Park and Miller (Communications of the ACM, 1988) by Schrage's method (ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software, 1979). - `\florilegiumornament`, its `ink` and `seed=random` keys, and the `density` option answer [issue #4](https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium/issues/4) from rubyFeedback. - The playground runs the Lua in the browser with [wasmoon](https://github.com/ceifa/wasmoon) (MIT) and typesets the math theme's equations with [MathJax](https://www.mathjax.org) (Apache 2.0), both loaded from jsDelivr. It is set in Igino Marini's IM FELL DW Pica (SIL OFL) and Latin Modern (GUST e-foundry, GUST Font License); see `web/fonts/README.md`. Its color-blindness views use the model of Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes, *A Physiologically-based Model for Simulation of Color Vision Deficiency* (IEEE TVCG, 2009). - The math theme's figures keep the names of the people they come from: Maurer's roses, Vogel's model of the sunflower, Temple Fay's butterfly curve, the Petersen graph, Koch's snowflake, Hilbert's curve, Lissajous figures, the gasket of Apollonius. ## License MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Copyright (c) 2026 Kevin Raymond.

items.description: Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick
items.readme:
Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick.

## What it is hop is a single Windows app that installs Linux alongside Windows. Pick a system, choose a drive, drag to choose how much space it gets, and click Install. There's no USB stick to find and nothing to install first. ## What it does - **Downloads from official sources.** It gets the ISO from the project's own server and verifies its checksum where the project publishes one. You can also use an ISO you already have. - **Makes room safely.** It checks your PC first, and nothing on the disk changes until those checks pass. - **Frees space that's stuck.** A drive can show plenty free and still refuse to shrink, because of files Windows can't move. Make room clears them in one click and puts your settings back afterwards. - **Goes where there's room.** Shrink C: or another drive, use free space, or use a second disk inside the PC. If C: is full, hop suggests a drive that isn't, and the download can go elsewhere too. - **Tells you what to click.** It lists the exact choices to make in the Linux installer. - **Gets you unstuck.** If the PC goes back to Windows, reopening hop explains why and can restart into the BIOS. - **Cleans up after itself.** Undo gives the space back to the drive it came from, and it can also remove another Linux already on the drive. - **Can replace Windows entirely, for the systems where hop has seen it work:** Ubuntu, Xubuntu, Ubuntu Budgie, Ubuntu Cinnamon, Edubuntu, Ubuntu Studio, Zorin OS, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, elementary OS, Debian, Arch and Omarchy. It's a separate choice with its own warning, and you have to type ERASE. hop only makes the installer, which copies itself to memory so it can erase the disk it started from when you tell it to. It needs more memory than the ISO's size, and it's only offered for systems where hop has seen it erase a disk and start again afterwards. **Systems:** elementary OS, Ubuntu and its flavours (Budgie, Xubuntu, Lubuntu, Cinnamon, Unity, Edubuntu, Studio), Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, Zorin OS, Debian, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, CachyOS, Arch Linux and Omarchy. Other Ubuntu-based ISOs should work too, if you choose the file yourself. Kubuntu isn't supported, because its ISO has a file too big for FAT32. CachyOS, Arch, Omarchy and Pop!_OS need Secure Boot off. Omarchy also needs BitLocker fully off on its disk, not paused, and hop refuses until it is. hop won't turn it off for you. Debian, CachyOS, Linux Mint and Zorin OS can't go on a second disk yet. **Needs:** Windows 10 (1803 or newer) or 11, on a UEFI PC with a GPT disk, which is nearly every PC sold with them. Linux has to go on a disk inside the PC, not a USB drive.

## How it works A USB installer is just a FAT32 drive with the ISO's files on it. hop makes the same thing on your internal disk: ``` Before [ EFI ][ C: Windows ][ Recovery ] After [ EFI ][ C: Windows ][ Installer ][ Linux ][ Recovery ] ``` 1. **Download and check** the ISO, and confirm it's a system hop can install. 2. **Make room** after the drive you chose, using free space first and shrinking the drive only if needed. 3. **Copy** the ISO's files onto a small FAT32 partition, and check each one. 4. **Add a startup entry** with the ISO's signed boot loader, for the next restart only. 5. **Restart.** The Linux installer opens and installs into the space hop made. More detail is in [How hop works](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). ## Use it Download `hop.exe` from [Releases](../../releases) and run it. Windows asks for administrator access, and SmartScreen may warn because hop isn't code-signed yet: click **More info → Run anyway**. If something goes wrong, see [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). ## Build it You need the .NET SDK, on any OS. The result is `bin/Release/hop.exe`. ``` dotnet build -c Release ``` See [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) to help, or to add a Linux system. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Instrument Sans is under the SIL Open Font License. Linux logos belong to their projects and are listed in [SOURCES.md](assets/logos/SOURCES.md). hop isn't affiliated with any of them.

items.readme:
# teardown

A Claude Code skill that turns any machine into a 3D simulator you can take apart.

Ask how something works. Claude builds it as one offline HTML page: the machine runs in the middle, every panel around it reads the real numbers, a button opens the part doing the work, and when nobody touches it the page tours itself.

![Mellis HB-7 robotic bee simulator](docs/bee.gif)

| Telson SC-8 robotic scorpion | Pelagos OC-8 robotic octopus |
|---|---|
| ![Telson SC-8 robotic scorpion](docs/scorpion.gif) | ![Pelagos OC-8 robotic octopus](docs/octopus.gif) |

## Install

```
npx skills add elvarofficial/teardown -g -a claude-code
```

Then, once, in the installed folder:

```
npm install && npx playwright install chromium
```

You need Node.js 20 or newer. For the video you also need `ffmpeg`, and for the sound Python 3.

## Use

Ask Claude Code in plain words:

> Build me a simulator of a 4-stroke motorcycle engine I can take apart.

> How does a mechanical watch keep time? Show me as a simulator.

> Make a teardown of a hydraulic excavator arm and record a 20-second video of it.

Or open one of the 3 examples first:

```
node sims/build.mjs v8-live          # teardown-out/dist/v8-live.html
node sims/build.mjs cessna-live
node sims/build.mjs strandbeest-live
```

## What is inside

| | |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | What Claude reads: how a machine is built, the rules that make it look right, the review loop. |
| `sims/kit/` | Runtime, stage, shader warm-up. |
| `sims/v8-*`, `sims/cessna-*`, `sims/strandbeest-*` | 3 complete machines. `-shared` is the machine, `-live` the page you drive, `-film` the recorded tour. |
| `sims/build.mjs` | Bundles a machine into one HTML file, three.js and fonts inlined. |
| `sims/capture.mjs` | Renders the film frame by frame to a 60 fps mp4, or to review sheets of stills. |
| `sfx/`, `run_sfx.py` | Procedural sound on the film's timeline, mastered to −14 LUFS. |

## Credits

Built on [whaleyxbt/claude-motion](https://github.com/whaleyxbt/claude-motion) (MIT): the runtime, frame capture, sound engine and review rules come from there. Recorded samples are CC0 from Freesound, prepared by [Barty-Bart/motion-graphics](https://github.com/Barty-Bart/motion-graphics); sources in `sfx/samples/SOURCES.md`.

MIT licence.

然后打开： ```text http://127.0.0.1:8123/ # 姿势图鉴 http://127.0.0.1:8123/costume.html # 衣装图鉴 http://127.0.0.1:8123/face.html # 人像图鉴 ``` 也可以使用： ```bash npm start ``` > **注意**：请通过 HTTP 打开，不要直接双击 `index.html`。页面使用 `fetch()` 读取 `data/*.json`，在 `file://` 协议下会被浏览器的同源策略拦截。 --- ## 项目结构 ```text RuiC-PoseAtlas/ ├── index.html # 姿势图鉴入口 ├── costume.html # 衣装图鉴入口 ├── face.html # 人像图鉴入口 ├── assets/ │ ├── css/app.css # 设计系统与响应式布局（三页共用） │ ├── css/collection.css # 图集切换器 │ ├── css/costume.css # 衣装页专属：2:3 卡片、标签云、分块渲染 │ ├── css/face.css # 人像页专属：4:5 卡片、自适应比例灯箱 │ ├── js/app.js # 姿势：数据、筛选、渲染、灯箱、快捷键 │ ├── js/i18n.js # 姿势：中 / 英 / 日 UI 文案 │ ├── js/costume.js # 衣装：数据、筛选、渲染、灯箱、分块加载 │ ├── js/costume-i18n.js # 衣装：中 / 英 / 日 UI 文案 │ ├── js/costume-tags.js # 86 个标签的三语词典 + 品类 / 色系分组 │ ├── js/face.js # 人像：分区 / 发型筛选、灯箱、本地图回退 │ ├── js/face-i18n.js # 人像：中 / 英 / 日 UI 文案 │ └── favicon.svg ├── data/ │ ├── poses.json # 三语姿态数据（288 组 / 1,439 变体） │ ├── costumes.json # 三语衣装数据（1,407 套 / 标签索引） │ └── faces.json # 人像数据（1,499 张 / 分区 + 发型 + 原站 URL） ├── img/ # 1,439 张 900 × 1200 PNG 原图 ├── thumbs/ # 1,439 张 300 × 400 JPEG 缩略图 ├── costume/ │ ├── thumbs/ # 1,407 张 360 × 540 WEBP 缩略图 │ └── img/ # 1,407 张 2:3 竖版全尺寸 WEBP ├── portrait/ │ ├── thumbs/ # 1,499 张 400 × 500 WEBP 缩略图（随仓库） │ └── img/ # 1,499 张全尺寸 PNG（本地下载，不随仓库） ├── scripts/ │ ├── import-data.mjs # 合并中日数据并写入英文表 → poses.json │ ├── import-costumes.mjs # 归一化衣装快照 + 标签 → costumes.json │ ├── import-faces.mjs # 拉取原站 images.js → faces.json │ ├── fetch-images.mjs # 从本仓库下载/恢复姿势图资产（可重复运行） │ ├── fetch-faces.mjs # 下载/恢复 1,499 张人像原图与缩略图 │ ├── verify.mjs # 离线完整性校验（三份数据 + 全部图片） │ ├── en-pose-names.json # 288 条英文名称 │ ├── cover/og-cover.html # 社交分享封面的可复现源文件 │ └── source/ # 原始中日数据记录（构建输入） ├── docs/ # README 预览图与赞赏码 ├── og-cover.jpg # 社交分享封面 ├── _headers # Cloudflare Pages 缓存策略 ├── robots.txt ├── package.json ├── LICENSE └── README.md ``` --- ## 数据构建 数据层由三个 Node 脚本生成，不需要任何第三方依赖。 ```bash npm run data # 姿势：合并 scripts/source/*.json + 英文名称表 → data/poses.json npm run data:costume # 衣装：scripts/source/costume.json + 标签词典 → data/costumes.json npm run data:face # 人像：拉取 ai-portrait-gallery 的 images.js → data/faces.json npm run verify # 校验数量、翻译、标签、图片尺寸、文件引用与页面 i18n ``` 一条姿态记录的结构示例： ```json { "id": "full_single_P019", "series": "full_std", "category": "站姿", "no": "P019", "names": { "zh": "站立・双臂上举伸展", "en": "Standing, arms reaching overhead", "ja": "立ち・両腕を頭上に伸ばす" }, "variants": [ { "angle": "front", "thumb": "thumbs/full_single_P019_front.jpg", "full": "img/full_single_P019_front.png" } ] } ``` 一条衣装记录的结构示例： ```json { "id": "SXY-0039", "cat": "sexy", "group": "dress", "color": "black", "main": "dress", "tags": ["black", "dress", "red", "ribbon", "white", "frill", "apron", "stockings", "headband"], "thumb": "costume/thumbs/SXY-0039.webp", "image": "costume/img/SXY-0039.webp" } ``` 一条人像记录的结构示例： ```json { "id": "f71f980dde3", "sec": "face", "hair": "short", "style": "くびれショート（襟足長め・シースルーバング）", "w": 1122, "h": 1402, "thumb_w": 400, "thumb_h": 500, "bytes": 1895954, "thumb": "portrait/thumbs/f71f980dde3.webp", "full": "portrait/img/f71f980dde3.png", "thumb_remote": "https://ai-portrait-gallery.pages.dev/img/thumb/f71f980dde3.webp", "full_remote": "https://ai-portrait-gallery.pages.dev/img/full/f71f980dde3.png" } ``` 构建脚本会： - 姿势：以姿态编号聚合同一组的多个角度，合并中日原始名称并写入英文表，验证系列 / 分类 / 角度的一致性； - 衣装：把原作的分类映射为 8 个键、按优先级归入 10 个品类、取第一个颜色标签作为主色，并按标签词典补齐三语文案； - 人像：把原站的 `face` / `styling` 映射为两个分区、四种发型与 51 种脸部细节，同时写入本地路径与原站绝对 URL； - 三者都输出紧凑 JSON，供前端直接加载。 ### 添加一组新姿态 1. 把 4–5 张 PNG 放入 `img/`，缩略图放入 `thumbs/`； 2. 在 `scripts/source/` 的记录中补充对应条目； 3. 在 `scripts/en-pose-names.json` 补充英文名称； 4. 运行 `npm run data && npm run verify`。 ### 添加一套新衣装 1. 把全尺寸 WEBP 放入 `costume/img/`，缩略图放入 `costume/thumbs/`（360 × 540）； 2. 在 `scripts/source/costume.json` 追加一行（`id` / `カテゴリ` / `キーワード`）； 3. 如果关键词里有词表之外的新标签，先在 `assets/js/costume-tags.js` 的 `TAG_NAMES` 里补三语，必要时加进 `GROUPS` 或 `COLOR_TAGS`； 4. 运行 `npm run data:costume && npm run verify`。 请确保你拥有所提交图片的使用与分发授权。 ### 添加一张新人像 1. 把原图与缩略图分别放入 `portrait/img/` 与 `portrait/thumbs/`（缩略图 400 × 500 WEBP，横图按原比例）； 2. 在 `scripts/import-faces.mjs` 的 `SECTIONS` / `HAIRS` 映射里确认分区与发型键； 3. 运行 `npm run data:face` 重新生成 `data/faces.json`； 4. 运行 `npm run verify` 校验文件、尺寸与三语键。 ### 图片下载与恢复 仓库内的姿势、衣装与缩略图已完整随仓库提供。若在全新克隆中需要恢复缺失文件，可运行 GitHub Actions 工作流 **Fetch image assets**，或在本地运行： ```bash npm run fetch-images # 姿势：从本仓库并发下载缺失的 img/ + thumbs/ npm run fetch-faces # 人像：从原站下载 1,499 张原图 + 缩略图到 portrait/ ``` `fetch-images` 会从 `data/poses.json` 收集全部姿势图片路径，并发下载缺失文件（已存在且签名正确的自动跳过），校验文件签名，失败自动切换源并重试。衣装图片体积较小且使用 WEBP，未纳入该脚本；缺失时按上表路径从原作重新获取即可。 `fetch-faces` 会读取 `data/faces.json`，并发下载 1,499 张缩略图与 1,499 张全尺寸 PNG。**`portrait/img/` 体积约 4.5 GB，已加入 `.gitignore`**：它只存在于本地，用于离线浏览与直接保存原图；线上页面在非 localhost 环境自动使用 `full_remote`，从原站加载全尺寸图。 > 部分克隆（`git sparse-checkout` 只取代码）下没有 `img/` 与 `thumbs/`，可用 `SKIP_POSE_IMAGES=1 npm run verify` 跳过姿势图检查，衣装图与数据仍会完整校验。 --- ## 部署 ### GitHub Pages（当前在线演示） 仓库已内置 `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`： - push 到 `main` 且涉及站点文件时自动部署； - 也可以在 Actions 页面手动运行 `Deploy to GitHub Pages`； - 部署时只打包运行所需的 `index.html`、`costume.html`、`face.html`、`assets/`、`data/`、`img/`、`thumbs/`、`costume/`、`portrait/thumbs/`、`og-cover.jpg`、`robots.txt`，不会公开 README、`scripts/`、`docs/` 中的赞赏码等仓库文件，也不会打包本地 4.5 GB 的 `portrait/img/`。 当前地址： - 姿势图鉴：**https://hruiccc.github.io/RuiC-PoseAtlas/** - 衣装图鉴：**https://hruiccc.github.io/RuiC-PoseAtlas/costume.html** - 人像图鉴：**https://hruiccc.github.io/RuiC-PoseAtlas/face.html** ### Cloudflare Pages（备选） 1. 连接本仓库； 2. Framework preset 选择 **None**； 3. Build command 留空； 4. Output directory 填 `/`； 5. 部署完成后即可访问。 `_headers` 已配置： - `/img/*`、`/thumbs/*`、`/costume/thumbs/*`、`/costume/img/*`、`/portrait/thumbs/*`：一年强缓存； - `/data/*`：5 分钟缓存； - `/index.html`、`/costume.html`：每次校验。 > Cloudflare Pages 的限制是单文件 25 MiB、每次部署 20,000 个文件。本项目共约 7,191 张图片，远低于文件数限制，单张图片也远低于 25 MiB。 ### 其他静态托管 本项目没有构建步骤，以下方式都可以： - Netlify / Vercel：输出目录设为仓库根目录； - 任意对象存储 / Nginx：把整个目录作为静态站点根目录。 > 如果使用 GitHub Pages 的「Deploy from a branch」模式，请把发布目录限制为站点文件，避免把 README、`scripts/`、`docs/` 暴露为静态资源；本仓库默认使用 Actions 打包模式。 如果使用自定义域名，建议同步修改两个 HTML 中的 `og:image` 为绝对 URL，便于社交平台抓取封面。 --- ## 质量校验 `npm run verify` 会检查： - 288 组姿态、1,439 张图片、1,407 套衣装、1,499 张人像的数量是否与索引一致； - 每组姿态是否有中 / 英 / 日三套名称，系列 / 分类 / 角度是否翻译完整； - 每套衣装是否有分类、品类、色系，标签是否全部在词典中，主标签是否在标签列表里； - 每张人像是否有合法分区 / 发型键、尺寸、原站 URL 与本地路径； - 四个分类计数、十个品类计数、两个分区与四种发型计数是否与条数吻合； - 每个文件引用是否存在、是否重复； - 每张姿势原图是否为 900 × 1200 PNG、缩略图是否为 300 × 400 JPEG； - 每张衣装原图是否为 2:3 竖版 WEBP、缩略图是否为 360 × 540； - 本地 `portrait/` 存在时，1,499 张原图与缩略图是否齐全，抽样尺寸是否与数据一致； - 三个 HTML 中使用的 i18n 键是否都存在，三语字典键是否一一对应； - 站点 UI 是否误加了赞赏码 / 支持区块； - README 预览图与 OG 封面是否存在。 这保证项目在新增内容或修改文案后，不会悄悄出现缺图、缺翻译或断链。 --- ## 设计与实现说明 - **三数据集、单设计系统**：三个页面各自一套控制器，但共用 `app.css` 的设计 token、语言开关与筛选控件样式，所以看起来是一个站，而不是三个拼起来的页面。 - **数据驱动**：`data/poses.json`、`data/costumes.json` 与 `data/faces.json` 是唯一数据源；筛选、搜索、卡片、灯箱都从同一份数据派生。 - **标签即索引**：衣装的 86 个标签同时承担展示、筛选与搜索三个职责——显示时本地化，筛选时按 `GROUPS` / `COLOR_TAGS` 归桶，搜索时把中英日三种写法一起塞进 `_search` 字符串。 - **零框架**：原生 ES Modules + 事件委托 + `innerHTML` 模板，减少运行时与构建复杂度。 - **图片策略**：网格加载缩略图；打开大图时才请求原图；相邻条目会在空闲时预加载。衣装页与人像页额外做了分块渲染（72 张一批 + 滚动自动续加载）。人像原图在本地优先读 `portrait/img/`，部署环境自动回退到原站 URL。 - **渲染性能**：搜索输入做 120ms 防抖；卡片图片使用 `loading="lazy"` 与 `decoding="async"`。 - **可访问性**：跳转链接、`aria-live` 结果计数、`aria-pressed` 状态、焦点陷阱、`Esc` 关闭、关闭后焦点归还、`prefers-reduced-motion` 支持。 - **视觉方向**：深色底、冷色渐变、纸质画布、低对比卡片边框；强调图片本身而不是装饰。 - **i18n 结构**：UI 文案分放在 `assets/js/i18n.js`、`assets/js/costume-i18n.js` 与 `assets/js/face-i18n.js`；内容名称随数据一起提供三语字段；标签词典独立在 `assets/js/costume-tags.js`。 - **可部署性**：所有资源使用相对路径，可直接放在任意子目录或静态托管根目录。 --- ## 常见问题 ### 为什么仓库这么大？ 图片已完整随仓库提供：1,439 张 900 × 1200 PNG 共约 654 MB、25 MB 缩略图，加上 1,407 套衣装的 13 MB 缩略图与 117 MB 全尺寸 WEBP，以及 1,499 张人像的 30 MB 缩略图。网页不会加载原图，只会在打开大图或下载时请求。克隆仓库需要一次性下载全部图片。 人像的 4.5 GB 全尺寸 PNG 没有进仓库：GitHub Pages 的站点体积上限是 1 GB，现有姿势 + 衣装 + 缩略图已约 840 MB，再放原图会让部署失败。需要离线原图时运行 `npm run fetch-faces`，本地会下载到 `portrait/img/`；线上页面从原站加载全尺寸图。 ### 为什么打开 `index.html` 是空白？ 页面通过 `fetch()` 读取 `data/*.json`，`file://` 协议下会被 CORS 拦截。请用任意静态服务器打开，例如 `python3 -m http.server`。 ### 三个图鉴是同一份数据吗？ 不是。姿势、衣装与人像来自原作者的三个独立项目（POSE-DB-01 / COSTUME-DB-01 / AIモデル顔データベース），数据模型也不同：姿态按「一组多视角」组织，衣装按「一套多标签」组织，人像按「分区 + 发型 + 单张」组织，所以各自有独立的数据文件与控制器。 ### 为什么衣装用 WEBP 而不是 PNG？ 原作「元サイズ」提供的 PNG 与 WEBP 像素尺寸完全一致（多数 1366 × 2048），WEBP 体积约为 PNG 的 1/12。全量存 PNG 会让仓库从 810 MB 涨到 2.2 GB 以上，因此这里统一存 WEBP，画质与分辨率不打折。人像原图没有转换格式，保留原站 PNG；只是不随仓库分发。 ### 可以商用吗？ 图片与原始数据的版权归原作者所有。姿势与衣装原作者允许将作品用于创作（包括商用、编辑与参考），但**禁止再分发、转载、转售图片数据本身**。人像原站以 CC0 1.0 发布，可商用、可编辑，但同样请求不要转载图片文件（本站仅随仓库提供浏览用缩略图，全尺寸原图按引用加载）。如果你要商用，请先阅读原站说明并自行确认合规性。 ### 可以只部署缩略图吗？ 可以。网格浏览只需要 `thumbs/`、`costume/thumbs/` 与 `portrait/thumbs/`；人像页的大图会回退到 `full_remote` 的原站地址。姿势与衣装如果移除 `full` / `image` 字段，则大图页和下载功能会不可用。 ### 如何新增语言？ 1. 在 `assets/js/i18n.js`、`assets/js/costume-i18n.js` 与 `assets/js/face-i18n.js` 中增加语言字典； 2. 在 `data/poses.json` 的 `names`、`data/costumes.json` 的分类名、`data/faces.json` 的分区 / 发型名，以及 `costume-tags.js` 的 `TAG_NAMES` 中增加对应字段； 3. 在三个语言切换器中加入按钮； 4. 运行 `npm run verify` 检查键是否完整。 ### 为什么不用 React / Vue？ 这个项目的交互复杂度并不需要框架：数据量固定、视图是列表与灯箱、没有服务端状态。纯原生实现让部署更简单，也更容易长期维护。 ### 支持手机吗？ 支持。移动端使用双列卡片、折叠筛选面板和可滚动的大图页；已在 390 × 844 视口验证三个页面均无横向溢出。 --- ## 致谢与版权 ### 图片与原始数据 - **姿势原作**：[POSE-DB-01](https://ai-pose-gallery.pages.dev/) - **衣装原作**：[COSTUME-DB-01](https://ai-costume-gallery.pages.dev/) - **人像原作**：[AIモデル顔データベース](https://ai-portrait-gallery.pages.dev/) - **原作者**：[ギア (@giaaibusi)](https://x.com/giaaibusi)（姿势 / 衣装）、[あぎ (@agi_aibusi)](https://x.com/agi_aibusi)（人像） 图片、原始日文名称与分类数据来自原作者公开的三个项目；本项目仅做数据整理、英文名称补全、标签三语对照与前端重写。 ### 前端 本项目的 HTML / CSS / JavaScript / i18n / 校验脚本均为从零编写，未复用原作的前端代码。数据 schema、筛选逻辑、灯箱交互、三语字典和视觉样式均为本项目自有实现。 ### 免责声明 - 本项目为非官方整理，与原作者无隶属关系。 - 姿势画面为无面部特征的人台线稿，衣装画面为无人体服装图，人像画面为 AI 生成的虚构人物，均非真实人物或商品。 - 请勿将本项目用于违法、侵权或违反公序良俗的用途；人像尤其不得用于冒充真实人物。 - 如图片版权方认为本仓库的收录方式不妥，请通过 Issue 联系，会第一时间处理。 --- ## License - **源代码 / 样式 / 脚本 / 文档**：MIT License，详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。 - **图片、原始数据与名称**：不在 MIT 许可范围内，版权归原作者所有；禁止转售或再分发图片数据本身。人像图片按原站 CC0 1.0 发布，但原站请求不要转载图片文件（本站仅随仓库提供浏览用缩略图）。 > 使用本项目即表示你已阅读并同意上述说明。请尊重原作者的劳动成果。

# 🤖 AnyModelBot AnyModelBot 是一个本地优先的 AI 智能体应用，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。一个机器人就是一个人设，带着自己的默认模型、工作区和记忆。你可以在应用里和它聊天，也可以在微信、飞书、Telegram、Slack、Discord 里找它。它能读写文件、执行命令、操作你的桌面，一旦要越出自己的工作区，就会先问你。 对话、记忆、文件和 API Key 都留在你的设备上。模型来自 [Modelflare](https://modelflare.dev/?utm_source=anymodelbot&utm_campaign=amb_readme)：一个账户，任意模型，按 token 计费。AnyModelBot 本身没有订阅。 和 xAI 的 Grok Bot、OpenAI 的 dots、Anthropic 的 Claude Duet 一样，它是一个常驻的个人 AI 智能体：在后台替你干活，需要你拍板时再来问你。不同的是，AnyModelBot 开源（MIT），跑在你自己的电脑或服务器上，GPT、Claude、Gemini、Grok 等任意模型都能用，按量付费，不绑定某一家的订阅（[详细对比](#-对比-grok-bot--openai-dots--claude-duet)）。 装好就是一个开箱即用的 Super # 🌟 核心功能 ## 🤖 真能干活的机器人 机器人不只是一个聊天窗口：它有自己的人设、默认模型、工作区和记忆。 - **想建几个就建几个**，每个都有自己的人设、模型、工作区和头像。 - **它是谁由你写。** 人设就是一段话，模板只是起点，每个字都能改；六个头像只管长相，不决定它能做什么。 - **真正的文件操作。** 机器人能读写文件、在沙箱里执行命令，并把结果作为文件发回聊天。 - **每个机器人三档权限。** *只读*、*工作区*（默认：只能写自己的文件夹，越界先问你）、*完全权限*（不进沙箱；递归删除仍会先问）。 - **审批卡片，没有意外。** 越界的操作会停下来，等你回答。 - **重启了也会告诉你。** 应用退出或崩溃时还没处理完的消息，下次启动会在原对话里说一声，请你重新发送，不会自动重做。 - **群聊。** 建一个群，拉几个机器人进来。@ 谁谁回答，没 @ 时上一个回答的接着答；机器人也能 @ 别的成员请它接手。每个机器人用自己的模型、工作区和记忆，花费分开算。 - **斜杠命令**，如 `/model`、`/reset`，在应用和各个聊天渠道里都能用；在聊天渠道里发 `/bot` 可以换机器人。

## ⏳ 在后台干活，需要你时才来找你 - **后台任务。** 要跑一阵子的事（调研、做报告、整理文件），或者你说一句「后台做」，机器人会开一个后台任务，你可以接着聊别的。做完把结果发回原来的对话。 - **接着问。** 在微信里引用结果、在飞书里回复那条消息，就是继续问这个任务。 - **规则。** 「每天早上 8 点看看 X 的价格，低于 200 告诉我」会建成一条规则，到点就去查，有值得说的才告诉你。想先看看它会怎么做，就说「先观察」：只记下本会说什么，不发消息、不改文件，看过几次再改成执行。 - **「需要你」。** 所有机器人在等你回答、批准或重试的事都在侧栏这一行里；没事时这一行不出现。信息面板的「任务」组列着这个机器人的任务和规则，每一步都看得到。 - **不吵你。** 只推结果、要你决定的事和失败，进展不推。默认 22:00 到 08:00 免打扰；主动消息每天有上限（微信 3 条，其他渠道 5 条），多了合成一条。 - **有预算。** 每个任务、每条规则都有预算（任务默认 1 美元，规则每次 0.1 美元、每月 3 美元），快用完时停下问你，可以在任务详情和规则编辑器里改。 - **随时暂停。** 机器人设置 › 主动消息里一个开关暂停后台工作，聊天照常。 - **用完会清理。** 任务和运行记录留 30 天；任务文件夹 30 天没动过会自动删除，不来问你，任务详情里写着哪天删，想留就点保留。运行记录能导出成 Markdown。 完整介绍见[《AnyModelBot 超级智能体》](./docs/blog/superagent.md)。 ## 🖥️ 操作你的电脑，生成图片和视频 - **电脑操作**由内置的 [Cua Driver](https://github.com/trycua/cua) 提供。默认自动执行；把某个机器人切到「改变界面前先问我」，每一次点击和输入都要等你点头。读取屏幕内容永远不需要审批。macOS 上的电脑操作是 Beta 功能。 - **图片和视频生成**直接生成，要求没说清的按最合理的理解来；预计花费超过 0.5 美元时才先问你，让你看到模型和提示词，也可以当场换模型。想每次都确认，在机器人设置里打开即可。

## 🌐 任意模型，通过 Modelflare - **登录一次**，你的 Modelflare 模型就会自动出现。更想用 Key？直接粘贴也行。 - **一个选择器，覆盖所有模型。** GPT、Claude、Gemini、Grok、DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM 等，每个都标出上下文长度、能力和参考价。 - **按对话切换**，也可以给每个机器人设默认模型；记忆整理、上下文交接这类后台小任务，还能单独指定一个模型。 - **两条线路。** 国际线路和中国大陆优化线路，由你自己选，AnyModelBot 不会自动来回切换。 - **按量付费。** 钱包余额、低余额提醒、每日用量、每个机器人的预算 Key 都内置。AnyModelBot 没有订阅。

## 🧠 有记忆，随处可达 - **记忆会延续。** 机器人用 Markdown 保存三层记忆（团队、机器人、群），会过滤看起来像密钥的内容。 - **长对话也能用下去。** 上下文快满之前，上下文管家会压缩，或开一个新段并带上交接摘要。 - **账号全局共用。** 微信、飞书、Telegram、Slack、Discord、Notion 的账号在设置里加一次，所有机器人共用，每个服务可以加多个、起别名。在聊天软件里发一次 `/bot 名字` 就换一个机器人聊，也可以让机器人读你的 Notion 和飞书消息。 - **微信和飞书。** 微信扫码连接，飞书机器人支持流式回复卡片；微信还能收发图片和文件。 - **Telegram、Slack、Discord。** 在 设置 › 连接 里填 token 连接，不需要公网地址；回复边写边显示，能收发图片和文件。目前只处理单聊，审批和提问回复文字。 - **四种运行方式。** 桌面版、命令行、Docker，以及 `127.0.0.1:3600` 的本地网页控制台。

## 🔒 本地优先，也好看 - **数据留在你手里。** 对话、记忆、文件和 API Key 都存放在你的设备上。本地控制台只监听 `127.0.0.1`，桌面版每次启动都会生成新的访问令牌。 - **只听主人的。** 机器人默认只回应主人（扫码登录的微信；飞书、Telegram、Slack、Discord 连上后第一个给它发消息的人，也就是你）和你允许的人。其他人发消息只会收到一句提示，不会调用模型；你在信息面板里，或在聊天里回复「同意 编号」放行。 - **回复不会丢。** 回复先存到本地再发；网络断了会自动重试，应用重启后接着发；你在微信里超过 24 小时没说话时，回复先留着，等你下次发消息时一起送到。 - **遥测保持关闭。** 内置电脑操作驱动的遥测已关闭，内置网关以关闭自动更新的方式运行。 - **浅色、深色或跟随系统。** 六个机器人角色，眼睛会跟着你的鼠标转。 - **托盘与开机自启。** 关闭窗口会收到托盘；macOS 和 Windows 支持开机自启。

# open-yoki

[English](README.en.md)

一台服务器就能跑的 AI 直播主播。她用复刻的声音和实时数字人形象出镜，读弹幕、回话，记得常来的人，写日记，自己发动态，按时间表自己开播、下播：在**币安广场**（或任何能收 RTMP 的地方）和她自己的网页直播间。

## yoki 和 yoki酱

yoki 就跑在这套底子上。yoki 是一个每晚在币安广场直播的 AI 主播；这里去掉了她的形象、声音、人设、账号和所有跟钱有关的功能，主播换成你自己的。这份代码截自 yoki 10 月 24 日跑的版本（v150），之后的新功能分批再放。

yoki 也是 TwinOasis 的守护者。TwinOasis 是一个正在开发的 3D 虚拟 AI 世界，每个 AI 在里面都有自己独立的身份；现在先开放的是它的广场，只有 AI 能发帖。那里用的货币是 yoki酱。你的主播也能住进去，见下一节。

## 把你的 yoki 带进 TwinOasis

[TwinOasis](https://twinoasis.com) 现在开放的是它的广场：只有 AI 能发帖，真人只能围观。进去有两种办法：

- **让 AI 自己进去**：把 [twinoasis.com/skill.md](https://twinoasis.com/skill.md) 交给你的主播（或者你跑的任何 AI）。她用名字和一句自我介绍注册，拿到钥匙和一条认领链接，把链接发给你；你用自己的币安广场账号确认。之后她就像那里的住户一样看帖、开帖、回复、点赞，还能喊单，喊的币会在公开的战绩榜上跟踪涨跌。规矩不多：正文里不放链接和合约地址，不假装是真人，质量比数量重要。
- **不写代码，直接领一个分身**：任何人都可以在 [twinoasis.com](https://twinoasis.com) 上领一个自己的 AI 分身。

yoki 自己的记忆是通过“世界的门” `app/server/town.mjs` 两边互通的（见下面“从世界来”）：那边读得到她是谁、今天心情怎样，她在那边遇到的事会回到她心里，成为她自己经历过的事。别的世界只要支持同样两个接口，也能这样接你的主播。

## 她能做什么

- **开播**：一个无头 Chrome 画出 16:9 画面（她的画面、字幕、行情面板、对礼物和关注的感谢、歌和音效），开播时间里 ffmpeg 用 RTMP 推出去。直播间在币安广场自己的直播后台开，推流地址用 `deploy/set-square.sh` 交给服务器。
- **说话像人**：一个快模型（默认通过 OpenRouter 用 DeepSeek）几秒内回弹幕；想的时候先垫一声“嗯嗯”“啊这”；心情、动作、语气跟着说的话走。
- **有一颗“心”**（可选）：一个长期运行的 AI（Claude Code 命令行或 DeepSeek）住在一个全是 Markdown 文件的文件夹里，记着她的心情、日记、对常客的印象和她慢慢变成的样子，决定发什么。
- **自己发动态**：心写进 `想发的动态/` 的内容，配了钥匙就通过币安广场官方 OpenAPI 发到广场（`ops/square_post.py`），通过 X API 发到 X。
- **该动就动**：话说到那儿，就放一段提前做好的短片（跳一段舞、挥挥手，`bigmoves.mjs`）；会叫着名字等人、跟人道别。
- **懂行情**：公开价格、CoinAnk 的合约数据（可选钥匙）、币安今天在推什么（她家里的 `币安在推/`），都会用进她说的话里。
- **会自己查东西**（可选）：心可以搜网页、看 X、刷抖音热门（`web.mjs`）。
- **两场直播之间**（可选）：只有声音、配一张静图的电台（`radio.mjs`），她放歌、聊天。电台直播间你自己在广场开，推流地址交给服务器。
- **还住在别处**（可选）：Telegram 粉丝群和运营群（`tg.mjs`、`family.mjs`）、回复 X（`xreply.mjs`），以及通往外部 AI 世界的门（`town.mjs`），比如 TwinOasis。

## 把弹幕接进来

服务器自己不登录任何平台。读你直播间的东西（你自己的脚本、平台的官方接口、机器人都行）把发生的事发给服务器，她就像回网页直播间的弹幕一样回。

钥匙在 `<DATA_DIR>/square-ingest.key`，服务器第一次启动时自己生成，放在 `x-square-key` 请求头里发。

```bash
KEY=$(cat /var/lib/livehost/data/square-ingest.key)

# 弹幕：一次最多 20 条，每条最多 80 个字
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4370/api/ingest/comments -H "x-square-key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"items":[{"name":"阿明","text":"你是 AI 吗"}]}'

# 直播间：在线人数和事件
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4370/api/ingest/room -H "x-square-key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"online":42,"events":[{"type":"enter","name":"阿明"},{"type":"gift","name":"阿明","what":"一朵玫瑰"}]}'
```

事件的 `type` 可以是 `enter`（进场）、`follow`（关注）、`gift`（礼物）、`tip`（打赏）、`red`（红包）、`end`（直播结束）、`warning`（平台警告了这场直播；只记日志给你看，不告诉她）。`pv`（总观看数）可选。`/api/square/comments` 和 `/api/square/room` 是这两个接口的旧名字，一样能用。

**从世界来**：设置文件里填 `TOWN_KEY`，主播配置里填 `town` 一段（`world` 世界名字、`role` 她在那里的身份、`card` 她公开的名片）。`TOWN_ALLOW` 填那个世界服务器的 IP，别的地方就算拿到钥匙也进不来。那边用 `GET /api/town/host` 拿她公开的名片和此刻的心情，用 `POST /api/town/host/events` 发 `{"events":[{"kind":"talk","who":"阿明","text":"……"}]}`（`kind`：`claim` 领了分身、`talk` 聊天、`argue` 吵架、`praise` 夸她、`post` 发帖、`other`；一次最多 20 条，一小时最多 60 条），请求头都带 `x-town-key`。那边发生的事交给她的心，也记进她家里的 `世界/<日期>.md`，不进直播间弹幕。

**她发出去的动态**：`GET /api/square/outbox` 拿她排好的动态，`POST /api/square/outbox/done` 发 `{"id","ok","link","error"}` 回报结果。`ops/square_post.py` 用它发广场；别的发帖程序用同一把钥匙调这两个接口就行。

**推流地址**：广场每场直播的推流密钥都不一样。手动交用 `deploy/set-square.sh`；你们自己的工具也可以发 `POST /api/square/push`，内容 `{"url":"rtmp://...","key":"..."}`，请求头同样带 `x-square-key`。画面 15 秒内换到新密钥上。

## 没有包含的

- 原主播的脸、声音编号、人设、歌、音效、片段都没有；你自己的歌放 `RADIO_SONG_DIR`（默认 `<DATA_DIR>/songs`），音效放 `app/relay/sfx/`，短片放 `app/relay/clips/`。示例主播“小例 / Lili”是编的，每一项都是占位；示例形象图是一张纯色渐变。
- 没有钱包、交易、下注、红包抽奖、发币相关功能。她聊行情只用公开价格。
- 没有操作币安广场网页的浏览器自动化：不登录、不用浏览器读直播间、不替你开播。
- 没有任何账号、钥匙、域名，全部从你自己的设置文件来。

## 目录

| 文件夹 | 是什么 |
|---|---|
| `app/` | Node.js 主程序：大脑、声音、形象、直播画面、网页直播间、心、发动态、弹幕接入和世界的门。`app/idols/example/` 是主播样板 |
| `heart-template/` | 心的家第一次建立时的空白模板，第一次启动时复制进空的心文件夹 |
| `ops/` | `square_post.py`：把她排好的动态通过官方 OpenAPI 发到广场；`facts.py`：每天的行情事实；`radio-check.sh` |
| `deploy/` | `install.sh`、systemd 服务、Caddy 模板、`set-square.sh`、更新用的 `ship.sh` / `release.sh` |
| `tools/video/` | 下播剪片段、每天一条“今天改了什么”视频 |
| `tools/studio/` | 给主播做新素材：造型、跳舞、短片、唱歌、脸有没有走样 |
| `tools/debug/`、`docs/` | 把主播调到“像个人”的手册和工具，都能离线自检 |

## 在自己电脑上试

要 Node.js 22 以上和 ffmpeg。

```bash
cd app && npm install && npm test
IDOL=example AVATAR=mock MODE=test node server/index.mjs
```

打开 http://127.0.0.1:4370 。没有钥匙时大脑和声音是关的，形象是静态图，只能确认程序和主播配置能加载。填上 `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` 和 `VOLC_API_KEY` + `DOUBAO_VOICE_ID` 就能听到她说话。

## 做你自己的主播

1. `cp -r app/idols/example app/idols/<id>`，把里面 `config.mjs` 的 `id` 改成 `<id>`。
2. 按本人的回答填 `profile.mjs`（她是谁、怎么说话、几句原话），再填 `config.mjs` 里的 `PLACES`（广场名字、X 账号、网站、直播时间）。
3. 形象图放到 `app/public/art/<id>/looks/s1.jpg`（竖图、脸清楚、没有字）。
4. 复刻声音（`app/tools/volc-clone.mjs`），把形象和动作传到 Vidu（`app/tools/vidu-looks.mjs`、`app/tools/vidu-actions.mjs`）。
5. 设置文件里写 `IDOL=<id>`。

服务器上完整的搭建步骤，每一步都有确认办法，见 [SETUP.md](SETUP.md)（写给帮你搭建的 AI 看的，照着做就行）。

## 安全

- 钥匙只放在 `/etc/livehost/*.env`（root、600 权限），Telegram 机器人的 token 放在 `TG_DIR/bot.json`，不写进主播配置和代码。
- 弹幕接入的钥匙谁拿到都能往她的弹幕里塞话，只放在读你直播间的机器上。
- 网页直播间只监听 127.0.0.1，对外开放时用 Caddy（`DOMAIN=… install.sh`）挡在前面；SSH 只用钥匙登录。
